data.title: Radium Music Editor
data.author: ofalkaed
data.article_summary: Radium是一款具有创新界面的音乐编辑器，相较于钢琴卷帘界面，其编辑速度更快，屏幕可容纳更多音乐数据。与追踪器界面相比，它支持图形化编辑音符位置和效果，提供更多垂直空间和更好的音乐数据可视化。Radium也是一款数字音频工作站（DAW），支持录音、编辑和混音，兼具文本编辑功能。自1999年开始开发，现已支持Linux、Windows和Mac。其功能包括多轨音频和MIDI、自动化参数、颗粒合成、平滑滚动、可选钢琴卷帘、无损变更缩放、微调音高、脚本编写、多核支持、无限撤销/重做等。Radium为开源软件，并提供Pure Data和Faust环境，支持多种插件格式。用户可以通过订阅支持其开发并获取优先更新。

主要讨论点：音乐追踪软件（trackers）的特性、使用体验及其与现代数字音频工作站（DAW）的比较

不同观点：
• **对追踪软件的热情与期待**：
   - **drannex** 表达了对具备线性时间线和自动化/调制效果的追踪软件的期待，提到曾考虑自己开发类似工具。
  
• **对软件稳定性和性能的质疑**：
   - **gbraad** 提到在Windows上使用该软件的体验不佳，软件运行缓慢且不稳定，尤其在加载OctaMED文件时遇到问题。尽管如此，他表达了对追踪软件的偏好，并提到自己有丰富的追踪软件使用经验。
  
• **追踪软件的历史与优势**：
   - **bane** 解释了追踪软件的历史和优势，强调其快速的工作流程和紧凑的多轨表示，适合快速迭代音乐创意。他还指出，追踪软件界面类似于编程，能让人更直接地接触音乐和乐器。

• **对具体功能和工具的兴趣**：
   - **Zambyte** 对软件中的Scheme脚本功能表示兴趣，询问其他人的使用经验。
   - **weinzierl** 对软件中使用LLVM技术表示好奇。

• **与其他DAW的比较**：
   - **RankingMember** 希望了解该追踪软件与Reaper的区别。
   - **brcmthrowaway** 询问该软件与Nodal的比较。
   - **ConanRus** 指出Renoise是最受欢迎的追踪软件之一。

补充讨论：
• **软件的实用性和社区支持**：
   - **bane** 提到大多数追踪软件是免费或非常便宜的，并且有丰富的文档和示例支持。
  
• **软件的开发状态和跨平台问题**：
   - **fabiofzero** 提到该软件的开发历时很长但稳定性一直是个问题，不过认为值得再次尝试。
   - **DidYaWipe** 提到Mac版本的问题，并表示如果理解追踪软件的界面可能会更感兴趣。
  
• **用户个人体验**：
   - **leothetechguy** 表示自己非常喜欢该软件，认为其值得购买。

• **历史参考和资源**：
   - **pvg** 提到2015年相关讨论线程。
   - **tenkabuto** 提供软件的使用手册和非官方视频教程链接。

• **对特定技术或工具的怀旧和支持**：
   - **bigfishrunning** 对s7 scheme工具的应用表示赞赏，认为其为程序添加了很好的脚本功能。

争议焦点：
• **软件的稳定性与跨平台兼容性**：部分用户（如gbraad）对Windows版本的性能和兼容性表示不满，而其他用户（如leothetechguy）则对软件表示高度赞赏，认为其值得购买。这种体验上的差异可能源于不同平台的技术实现问题。

About Radium
Radium is a music editor with a new type of interface.
Compared to the
piano roll interface
,
editing is quicker
and
more musical data fits on the screen
.
(Radium has a piano roll as well.)
Compared to the
tracker interface
,
note positions and effects can be edited graphically
. Graphical editing provides
more vertical space
and gives a
better visualization of musical data
.
(Everything can also be edited by text, like in a normal tracker, combining the best of two worlds.)
Radium is also a
Digitial Audio Workstation
(DAWg), which can be used to record, edit, and mix audio.
However, despite its unusual appearance, it's a design goal for Radium to be
straightforward to use, and easy to learn
.
It should not be harder to learn Radium than any tracker or most MIDI sequencers.
Users accustomed to trackers might use more time adjusting to the interface.
History
The development of Radium started in 1999 based on ideas developed 1997-1999 while extending the Octamed tracker on the Amiga.
The first public version of Radium was released in 2000.
Since then, Radium has been ported to Linux, Windows, and Mac.
Today, Radium is probably the worlds largest and most advanced tracker-like music editor.
Some of the features
Audio and MIDI multitracker
Automate pitch, velocity, effects, and tempo.
Granular synthesis
Smooth scrolling
Optional piano roll
Tickless
Global swing, and swing-per-track
Modular mixer and/or mixer strips
MIDI sequencing
Hard drive audio recording and playback
AU, LADSPA, LV2, VST, and VST3 plugins
(More than 100 LADSPA plugins are included)
Several built-in effects and instruments
(virtual instruments, multiband compressor, modulators, etc.)
Pure Data
embedded.
(Linux only for now)
Includes a
Faust
audio DSP development environment
Frame-accurately synchronize playback to e.g.
Ardour
,
Bitwig
, or
MASCHINE
.
Graphical zoom
Non-destructive changable Lines Per Beat ("Line Zoom").
Microtonality
Scripting in Python or Scheme.
Plugin delay compensation applied to all parts of the audio graph
Multicore support
Unlimited undo/redo
Open source with a straightforward and easy to use build system (no CMake or IDEs).
Quick start
Load a demo song from the File menu.
Play by pressing space.
Add a new note to the editor by pressing a key on the computer keyboard. Change octave with F1 and F2.
(Or record from MIDI input)
Look at the
manual.

data.title: Smollm3: Smol, multilingual, long-context reasoner LLM
data.author: kashifr
data.article_summary: SmolLM3是一款小型、多语言、支持长上下文推理的30亿参数语言模型，性能超越Llama-3.2-3B和Qwen2.5-3B，并可与40亿参数模型竞争。该模型支持6种语言，采用Transformer解码器架构，结合了Grouped Query Attention、NoPE等技术以提升效率和长上下文表现。通过三阶段预训练方法和混合推理模式，SmolLM3在多项任务中表现出色。其完整工程蓝图和训练方法已在GitHub上发布，包括架构细节、数据混合策略和训练配置，为开发者提供了详细的指导。模型训练使用了384块H100 GPU，耗时24天。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SmolLM3模型的性能、开源贡献、实际应用及技术挑战

不同观点：
• WhitneyLand：认为SmolLM3在3B级别达到了当前顶尖性能，并赞赏其完全公开模型、代码及训练方法，提供了一个可复现的框架。同时，指出训练成本较高，约需百万美元的GPU时间。
• lvl155：强调该模型对于初学LLM的人是一个很好的学习材料，有助于快速上手。
• gardnr：指出SmolLM3模型小巧但性能优异，特别适合边缘设备和移动部署，并提到其双模式推理功能和公开的完整训练方法，节省了反向工程的时间。
• danielhanchen：分享了修复chat模板问题的具体操作步骤，提供了技术上的帮助。
• simonw：遇到了在Mac上运行该模型的问题，尝试多种方法后仅能在CPU模式下运行，但速度很慢，寻求其他解决方案。
• _1：关注适合企业数据集微调的小模型，希望能够在浏览器和移动设备上运行而不依赖云资源。
• gdiamos：赞赏SmolLM3的同时，希望继续开发50-100M参数的模型，认为这些模型在CPU上快速完成任务有其价值。
• BarakWidawsky：指出SmolLM3未使用自有RL，而是通过大型数据集的推理痕迹进行微调，并从大型模型生成推理痕迹。
• msgodel：认为SmolLM3接近Qwen3的压缩版，质量很高，计划用于本地代理和代码补全，并提到自己的代码已过时，技术更新速度很快。
• eachro：询问SmolLM3的微调难度，与其他MoE LLMs的微调难度作比较。
• tiahura：好奇多语言支持占用了多少模型参数。
• grrowl：赞赏Huggingface在CodeEval和Python工具上的坚持，认为目前对LLM编写和执行代码的能力未被充分开发。
• ivape：质疑SmolLM3是否比OpenRouter上的llama 3.1 8b更便宜，并指出3B模型正被默认用于设备上，如Apple和Google的nano。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：SmolLM3在不同硬件和软件环境下的运行问题，特别是Mac上的运行挑战。
• 重要论据：SmolLM3的公开透明性、性能优势、在边缘设备和移动设备上的适用性、以及与其他模型的比较。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：模型的微调难度、多语言支持的参数占用、以及未来小参数模型的发展潜力。

Small language models are becoming increasingly important as users seek capable models that can be deployed efficiently. The community has produced a fascinating range of capable small models, each pushing the boundaries of what's possible at this scale. With SmolLM3, we're excited to contribute a new competitive fully open 3B model:
Base model:
https://hf.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-Base
Instruct and reasoning model:
https://hf.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B
SmolLM3 sits in the efficiency sweet spot.
Our 3B model outperforms Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B while staying competitive with larger 4B alternatives (Qwen3 & Gemma3). Beyond the performance numbers, we're sharing exactly how we built it using public datasets and training frameworks.
Model summary:
3B model
trained on 11T tokens, SoTA at the 3B scale and competitive with 4B models
Instruct model
with
dual mode reasoning,
supporting
think
/
no_think
modes
Multilingual support
for 6 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, and Portuguese
Long context
up to 128k with NoPE and using YaRN
The complete recipe:
We're releasing SmolLM3 with our engineering blueprint. It includes architecture details, exact data mixtures showing how we progressively boost performance across domains in a three-stage pretraining approach, and the methodology for building a hybrid reasoning model. Usually, achieving these results would require months of reverse engineering. Instead, we're providing the full methodology.
Whether you're building your own models or want to understand what drives performance at this scale, this blueprint shows the engineering story behind competitive 3B performance.
Let’s have a look at the pretraining stage.
Pretraining
SmolLM3 both changed the architecture and data mixture over its predecessors. Let’s have a look at the architecture and training configurations first!
Architecture and training details
SmolLM3 follows a transformer decoder architecture with tied embedding similar to SmolLM2, building on Llama architecture with some key modifications optimized for efficiency and long context performance.
Grouped Query Attention (GQA):
We replaced multi-head attention with grouped-query attention using 4 groups. Our ablations on a 3B model trained with 100B tokens from
FineWeb-Edu
showed that GQA matches the performance of multi-head attention while significantly reducing the KV cache size during inference.
NoPE:
We implemented NoPE from "
RoPE to NoRoPE and Back Again: A New Hybrid Attention Strategy
" (Yang et al., 2025), selectively removing rotary position embeddings from every 4th layer. This approach improves long context performance without affecting short context capabilities, as confirmed by our ablations.
Intra-Document Masking:
During training, we use attention masking to ensure tokens from different documents in the same training sequence don't attend to each other. Similar to Llama 3, this helps with faster and more stable long context training while maintaining short context performance.
Training Stability:
Following OLMo 2, we remove weight decay from embedding layers to improve training stability. This modification contributed to more stable training dynamics, with embedding norms naturally stabilizing at healthier values during training without impacting overall performance in our ablations.
All these changes were validated through ablations using the same 3B architecture trained on 100B tokens from FineWeb-Edu, ensuring each modification either improved performance or maintained it while offering other benefits.
Training Configuration: We use a global batch size of 2.36M tokens with 4096 sequence length, a learning rate of 2e-4, and the AdamW optimizer (beta1: 0.9, beta2: 0.95) with weight decay of 0.1 and gradient clipping of 1. We use the WSD (Warmup-Stable-Decay) scheduler, with 2000  warmup steps, and a linear decay to 0 in the final 10% training steps. We use
nanotron
framework for the training,
datatrove
for data processing and
lighteval
for evaluation. The model was trained on 384 H100 GPUs for 24 days. You can see the distributed training setup in the following figure.

• _1：关注适合企业数据集微调的小模型，希望能够在浏览器和移动设备上运行而不依赖云资源。
• gdiamos：赞赏SmolLM3的同时，希望继续开发50-100M参数的模型，认为这些模型在CPU上快速完成任务有其价值。

• tiahura：好奇多语言支持占用了多少模型参数。
• grrowl：赞赏Huggingface在CodeEval和Python工具上的坚持，认为目前对LLM编写和执行代码的能力未被充分开发。
• ivape：质疑SmolLM3是否比OpenRouter上的llama 3.1 8b更便宜，并指出3B模型正被默认用于设备上，如Apple和Google的nano。

data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者如何发现并利用一款名为Catwatchful的安卓间谍软件服务中的SQL注入漏洞，最终获取了超过6万个间谍用户账户的数据。作者首先通过注册一个免费试用账户，发现该服务同时在Firebase和一个自定义服务器上创建账户。在分析其流量后，作者注意到用户数据存储在Firebase中，难以直接攻击，但注册时涉及的另一个服务器（catwatchful.pink）存在SQL注入漏洞。通过利用该漏洞，作者成功获取了大量用户的敏感信息，揭示了该间谍软件在安全性上的重大缺陷。

Background

Recently I was looking through a database of known stalkerware services and found one I wasn’t familiar with:
Catwatchful
. It seemed to be a full-featured Android spy app, to actually be its own service as opposed to a millionth FlexiSpy reseller, and to offer a 3-day free trial. Aside from a boilerplate disclaimer to only use it with consent, it also pretty brazenly advertised itself as stalkerware in the FAQ:
Q: Can I monitor a phone without them knowing?
A: Yes, you can monitor a phone without them knowing with mobile phone monitoring software. The app is invisible and undetectable on the phone. It works in a hidden and stealth mode.
Apparently still unsatisfied, it boasted even further about “absolute stealth” in a list of features:
Catwatchful is invisible. It cannot be detected. It cannot be uninstalled. It cannot be stopped. It cannot be closed. Only you can access the information it collects.
Let’s see about that last part, shall we?
Part 0: Setup
#
I began by making a free trial account on the website. Interestingly, this triggered two separate POST requests:

It seems to have made me an account in both a Firebase instance and a custom database on
catwatchful.pink
.
After registration and login, I get given an APK to download and install. From here, installation goes as usual for Android stalkerware: the app has me download and install another APK pre-configured with my account credentials. This app then asks for basically every permission on the system, guides me through uninstalling the original installer app, then runs in the background forever while disguising itself in the app drawer with a generic “Settings” icon.
Part 1: Recon
#
After installing the app and re-logging into the web interface, I’m presented with a control panel with which to spy on my test phone. Two things stand out to me here: first of all, the app works really well. A lot of stalkerware apps are half-broken, clearly built by gluing together various chunks of spaghetti code long abandoned by their original authors. Not so here - all these features work as advertised with minimal latency. The live photo and microphone options are particularly creepy, successfully taking a photo or recording and uploading it for me to view near-instantly on the control panel without giving the phone user the slightest sign that anything is amiss.
The only bug I found was in the sidebar counters (I did not in fact take 3002 screenshots while testing)
The second notable thing is that all the personal data collected here seems to be stored in Firebase, served from Cloud Storage URLs in the form
catwatchful-e03b8.appspot.com/o/usersFiles/JIOgo826TPfb0pMFKmzkE7jz9JO2/M6GPYXHZ95ULUFD0/micRecorders/grab_2025-06-09_17-04-34
. Intercepting my test phone’s traffic confirms that the files are directly uploaded to Firebase, and reveals that the commands for features like live photos are also handled through FCM. This is going to reduce our attack surface by a lot - nothing in Firebase is going to be IDORable or vulnerable to SQLI, and some quick testing eliminates any of the usual traps like open storage buckets or client-side service account credentials. We’re going to have to focus on that mysterious
catwatchful.pink
server I was also signed up on.

data.article_summary: Rain Pomodoro是一款结合了雨声、棕噪音和ASMR触发器的工作专注计时器，旨在通过沉浸式音效和动态雨景动画提升专注力。它提供真实的雨声效果，包括风声、山间溪流和沙漠风暴，同时搭配棕噪音，能有效屏蔽干扰，增强注意力。ASMR音效帮助放松，减少压力荷尔蒙，提升工作效率。此外，中东风情的音乐和音景刺激创造性思维。计时器还支持自定义25分钟专注时间和休息提醒，配合电影级背景视觉效果，创造理想的专注环境。研究表明，棕噪音比白噪音更适合学习，能减轻精神疲劳。Rain Pomodoro通过科学设计，帮助用户在工作和学习中保持高效专注。

data.title: Rules of good writing (2007)
data.author: santiviquez
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于写作风格、简洁性、以及不同语言和文体对写作的影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• mtlynch: 认为读者理解“the boy hit the ball”比“the ball was hit by the boy”更快，因为英语中主语→动词→宾语的结构更常见。但怀疑这种理解方式可能仅适用于英语，并不一定适用于所有语言。
• kens: 提到大多数写作指南都是Strunk & White的复述，但推荐了"Style: Toward Clarity and Grace"作为更高级的选择。
• wduquette: 对纠正一个18年前的评论感到无奈，认为纠正过时的观点是徒劳的。
• raincole: 指出写作规则具有情境性，不同领域（如科技创业和文学杂志）对写作风格的要求不同，没有绝对的规则。
• CharlesW: 认为Strunk的“省略不必要的词”是好的商业写作建议，但对于想要深入写作 craft 的人，推荐Stephen King的《On Writing》。
• GGByron: 强调简洁不仅仅是去掉多余的词，还包括避免陈词滥调。认为Adams没有引用Orwell，也没有解释清楚概念。
• djoldman: 赞同简洁性，引用Hemingway的观点，认为应该删减句子中的多余词汇。
• irchans: 纠正mtlynch的评论，指出应该是“主语（the boy）在动作（the hitting）之前”，而不是“对象（the boy）”。
• Labov: 认为简洁的写作建议适用于博客作者和记者，但不一定适合小说家或诗人。
• m0llusk: 幽默地提到rap音乐的兴起是否与写作简洁性有关。
• jbreckmckye: 认为清晰和简短虽然是好的开始，但并不足够，还需要更多的修饰和内容。引用Calvin Coolidge的例子来说明过于简短的弊端。
• lutusp: 质疑“好写作的规则”这一说法，认为标题本身是一个词汇错误，应该关注的是选择而不是价值。提到Strunk & White的影响，并幽默地表示自己“煮掉”了这本书，只剩下“让每个词都有价值”这一点。
• CalChris: 认为Adams给出了好的建议，但过于简洁的写作可能不会让人记住作者。

补充讨论：
• 关于写作简洁性和规则的普遍适用性存在争议，不同文体和领域对写作风格的要求不同。
• 对Strunk & White的观点和影响有不同的评价，有人推荐更高级的写作指南。
• 评论中还涉及到对过时评论的无奈，以及对写作建议的幽默调侃。

争议焦点：
• 写作简洁性的适用范围和程度，特别是在不同文体和语言中的应用。
• 对传统写作规则的遵循与突破，以及这些规则是否真正有助于提升写作质量。

data.title: Xenharmlib: A music theory library that supports non-western harmonic systems
data.author: retooth
data.article_summary: Xenharmlib 0.3.0 是一个支持传统和非传统音乐理论的Python库，特别适用于非十二平均律系统的微音程和宏音程调音。它易于使用且可扩展，支持西方和非西方音阶系统、非标准记谱法以及音程、音阶的分析与调制建议。该库还提供对波尔-皮尔斯调音的群论分析等功能。Xenharmlib 并非用于乐谱编写或合成，而是专注于和声关系的科学探索，采用函数式编程原则，对象为不可变类型。未来计划包括支持更多记谱法、高级后调性分析和Just Intonation等。该库基于GNU Public License v3发布，源代码托管于Gitlab，并有Discord社区支持。

New Release
Xenharmlib 0.3.0 has just been released.
Find out what’s new
Welcome to xenharmlib’s documentation!
¶
Xenharmonic (adj.):
Pertaining to music which sounds unlike
that composed in the familiar 12 tone equal-tempered scale.
—
Ivor Darreg
Xenharmlib is a generalized music theory library that supports traditional
Western and non-western harmonic systems, unconventional microtonal and
macrotonal tunings, diatonic and posttonal set theory and non-standard
notations.

Audience & Design Philosophy
¶
Xenharmlib is targeted at composers and researchers who already have
basic knowledge in python programming.
Xenharmlib does
not
aim to be a score composition tool, sequencer,
or synthesizer (however it is possible to build such things on top of
it). Rather it wants to provide a toolset for exploring different
concepts of harmonic relations with a scientific focus.
Xenharmlib is object-oriented but mostly designed around functional
programming principles: Objects are considered immutable and methods
do not alter internal states but return modified versions of the
original object.
Features
¶
A selection of things supported by xenharmlib:
Equal division tunings (e.g. Western, Modern Arabic, Turkish Makam,
Bohlen-Pierce, Wendy Carlos’ Gamma Scale)
Western notation (including interval naming)
Up/Down notation (a superset of Western notation)
Analysis of intervals, scales, and their relations to one another
Group theoretical analysis (integer pitches, pitch classes, etc)
Interval sequence pattern matching
Modulation suggestions for arbitrary key changes
Basic posttonal analysis (normal & prime form calculations, inversion, etc)
Roadmap
¶
A list of planned features (not necessarily in chronological order):
Templates for Western music
Plugin interface for score rendering backends
Advanced posttonal analysis (interval vectors, z-Relations, Forte numbers)
Rothenberg propriety and interval matrices
MOS scale generation utilities
Just Intonation and prime limit tunings
Extended Helmholtz-Ellis JI Pitch Notation
Odd Limit Tunings
Arel-Ezgi-Uzdilek notation
License
¶
Xenharmlib is released under the
GNU Public License v3
.
You can find the source code hosted on
Gitlab.com
Acknowledgments
¶
Thanks to
Kite Giedraitis
and
Lumi Pakkanen
and everyone else on the
Xenharmonic Alliance Discord who was patient with me when I was
struggling to implement UpDownNotation.
Support and Contact
¶
If you want to ask for a new feature or report a bug, take it to the
Gitlab issue page
.
In case you just wanna chat with the maintainer: I often hang around on
the
Xenharmonic Alliance Discord
under the name
@retooth
User Guide
¶
In the following, you will find a guide to most of xenharmlib’s
features.

data.title: Bulgaria to join euro area on 1 January 2026
data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 保加利亚将于2026年1月1日加入欧元区，汇率定为1.95583列弗兑1欧元。保加利亚于2020年加入欧盟汇率机制（ERM II），其货币汇率自那时起一直保持在该水平。自2020年10月1日起，欧洲央行（ECB）开始直接监管保加利亚的四家主要金融机构，并 oversight 其他13家较小机构。保加利亚在ERM II中的表现符合加入欧元区的趋同标准，ECB和保加利亚国民银行将共同监控其汇率直至2026年。媒体咨询联系人：Benoit Deeg，电话：+49 172 1683 704。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧元区的扩张及其影响

不同观点：
• 支持欧元扩张的观点：
   - 欧元作为单一货币已经成功运行了26年，并且仍在扩展（decimalenough）。
   - 欧元帮助各国以较低利率获得贷款，减少货币市场不稳定的风险（16th_hop）。
   - 欧元在减少美元主导地位方面具有积极意义（v5v3）。

• 对欧元扩张持怀疑或批评的观点：
   - 担心欧元区国家经济实力不同，统一货币和中央管理并不理想（v5v3）。
   - 希腊的教训：加入欧元区可能导致经济困境，特别是无法通过货币贬值来缓解经济问题（ktsangop）。
   - 引入欧元可能导致物价显著上涨，类似情况曾在其他国家发生过（theodric, jmyeet, storus）。

• 对欧元实际影响的讨论：
   - 欧元在日常生活中并未带来太大变化，但其象征意义和政治意义重大（SwtCyber）。
   - 一些用户担心旅游业的发展可能导致地方独特性的丧失（keiferski）。

补充讨论：
• 关于欧元引入后物价变化的研究不足，历史上的转换如德国和法国的经验值得参考（jmyeet）。
• 欧元购买力下降的问题，以及通过电视广告宣传引入欧元的必要性受到质疑（ingohelpinger）。

争议焦点：
• 欧元引入对经济的长远影响，特别是对新加入国家如保加利亚的经济影响存在争议。一方面是经济整合和贷款成本降低的优势，另一方面是物价上涨和经济自主性丧失的风险。

PRESS RELEASE
Bulgaria to join euro area on 1 January 2026
8 July 2025
Conversion rate of lev fixed at 1.95583 = EUR 1
Bulgaria joined the ERM II in 2020
Bulgarian banks supervised by ECB since 2020
Today the Council of the European Union formally approved the accession of Bulgaria to the euro area on 1 January 2026 and determined a Bulgarian lev conversion rate of 1.95583 per euro. This is the current central rate of the lev in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM II), which the currency joined on 10 July 2020. The European Central Bank (ECB) and Българска народна банка (Bulgarian National Bank) agreed to monitor developments in the Bulgarian lev against the euro on the foreign exchange market until 1 January 2026.
With the entry into force of the
close cooperation framework between the ECB and Българска народна банка (Bulgarian National Bank)
, the ECB has been responsible for directly supervising four significant institutions and overseeing 13 less significant institutions in Bulgaria since 1 October 2020.
For media queries, please contact
Benoit Deeg
, tel.: +49 172 1683 704.
Notes
The agreement to monitor the lev is in the context of ERM II. Participation in ERM II and observance of the normal fluctuation margins for at least the last two years is one of the convergence criteria to be fulfilled ahead of euro area accession.
The conversion rate of the lev is set by way of an amendment to Regulation (EC) No 2866/98, which will become effective on 1 January 2026.

data.title: RapidRAW: A non-destructive and GPU-accelerated RAW image editor
data.author: l8rlump
data.article_summary: RapidRAW是一款现代、高性能、非破坏性的RAW图像编辑器，支持GPU加速，体积小巧（不到30MB），适用于Windows、macOS和Linux。它由CyberTimon开发，旨在为摄影工作流提供高效工具，同时加深对React和Rust的理解。其核心功能包括GPU加速处理、AI驱动的遮罩、广泛的RAW格式支持、非破坏性编辑、32位精度、专业的调整工具（如色调控制、颜色分级、细节增强等）、以及高效的图像库管理。近期更新包括增强的AI功能、图像评分过滤器、预设覆盖、以及对ComfyUI的初步集成。项目采用AGPL-3.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于开源RAW图像处理工具“RawTherapee”的评价与讨论，涉及功能、性能、用户体验、技术细节等方面。

不同观点：
• **对RawTherapee的积极评价**：
   - strogonoff：赞赏其色彩科学准确性、可脚本化、丰富的文档（RawPedia），尤其适合对技术细节感兴趣的用户。同时也指出其缺少HDR输出的问题。
   - miladyincontrol：希望加入亮度蒙版功能，认为这对RAW编辑非常重要。对现有的AI主体蒙版功能表示赞赏。
   - ioma8：表示有兴趣参与该项目的开发。

• **性能问题的反馈**：
   - polishdude20：在M1 Mac上运行时，初次加载卡顿严重，虽然之后有所改善，但整体不够流畅。
   - vsviridov：在Windows 10和AMD RX 6900 XT上运行时，处理6000x4000的DNG文件速度很慢，调整参数时延迟明显。

• **对元数据和跨平台支持的关注**：
   - pradn：关心元数据的存储方式，尤其是是否为开放格式，以便在不同程序间迁移编辑内容。同时提到不愿每月付费订阅Lightroom。
   - rkagerer：询问系统要求和最低操作系统版本。

• **对用户界面和技术实现的讨论**：
   - dxroshan：认为基于网页的图像编辑界面不好，会慢且资源消耗大。
   - Springtime：赞赏README中的视觉概览，但指出GIF文件过大，建议使用视频代替以提高加载速度。
   - bjelkeman-again：询问Mac代码签名的难度。

• **对RAW和Bitmap区别的疑问**：
   - brcmthrowaway：询问RAW和Bitmap的区别，特别提到Bitmap是否无压缩。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户对RawTherapee的技术细节表现出浓厚兴趣（如色彩科学、元数据处理、默认相机和镜头配置文件等），而另一些用户则更关注实际使用中的性能问题（如卡顿、延迟）。
• 关于跨平台支持和系统要求的问题也被多次提及，显示出用户群体对软件兼容性和易用性的关注。
• 部分用户对RawTherapee与商业软件（如Capture One、Lightroom）的对比，反映出开源与商业软件之间的选择争议。

RapidRAW
A beautiful, non-destructive, and GPU-accelerated RAW image editor built with performance in mind.
RapidRAW is a modern, high-performance alternative to Adobe Lightroom. It delivers a feature-rich, beautiful editing experience in a lightweight package (under 30MB) for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
I developed this project as a personal challenge at the age of 18. My goal was to create a high-performance tool for my own photography workflow while deepening my understanding of both React and Rust, with the support from Google Gemini.
Have fun!

Key Features
Core Editing Engine
GPU-Accelerated Processing:
All image adjustments are processed on the GPU using a custom WGSL shader for rapid feedback.
Masking:
Instantly create precise masks with AI subject and foreground detection. Combine with traditional Brush, Linear, and Radial masks for great control.
Generative Edits:
Remove objects or add new elements with text prompts. Each edit creates a non-destructive patch layer, powered by an optional ComfyUI backend.
Full RAW Support:
Supports a wide range of RAW camera formats thanks to rawler.
Non-Destructive Workflow:
All edits are stored in a
.rrdata
sidecar file, leaving your original images untouched.
32-bit Precision:
Ensures high-quality adjustments without banding or data loss.
Professional Grade Adjustments
Tonal Controls:
Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, and Blacks.
Tone Curves:
Full control over Luma, Red, Green, and Blue channels.
Color Grading:
Temperature, Tint, Vibrance, Saturation, and a full HSL color mixer.
Detail Enhancement:
Sharpening, Clarity, Structure, and Noise Reduction.
Effects:
Dehaze, Vignette, and realistic Film Grain simulation.
Transform Tools:
Crop with aspect ratio locking, Rotate, and Flip.
Library & Workflow
Image Library:
Effortlessly sort, rate, and manage your entire photo collection for a streamlined and efficient workflow.
Folder Management:
Integrated folder tree, create, rename, and delete folders directly within the app.
File Operations:
Copy, move, and duplicate images and their associated edits.
Filmstrip View:
Quickly navigate between all the images in your current folder while editing.
Batch Operations:
Save significant time by applying a consistent set of adjustments or exporting entire batches of images simultaneously.
EXIF Data Viewer:
Gain insights by inspecting the complete metadata from your camera, including shutter speed, aperture, ISO, and lens information.
Productivity & UI
Preset System:
Create, save, import, and export your favorite looks.

data.title: Frame of preference A history of Mac settings, 1984–2004
data.author: K7PJP
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了1984年至2004年间Mac电脑设置界面的演变历史。作者作为一名设计师，虽然按理应不喜欢设置选项，但作为用户却对其充满兴趣，并每年设立“设置日”来研究软件中的选项和开关。文章特别提到1984年由Susan Kare设计的Mac控制面板，这一设计至今仍被提及。最初的控制面板简洁直观，包含了动画和早期GUI实验元素，如滑块和步进器。有趣的是，当时团队对桌面定制功能存在分歧，担心用户会创建“丑陋的桌面图案”。尽管存在一些小瑕疵和操作缓慢的问题，早期控制面板依然充满魅力。到了1986年，随着时间推移，许多原有的 charm 逐渐消失。文章通过回顾Mac设置界面的发展，展示了这台机器早期历史和设计挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕一篇关于Mac电脑和操作系统模拟器的文章展开，涉及技术实现、用户体验、怀旧情感以及对现代系统设置的批评。

不同观点：
• [赞赏技术实现] 
  - thristian: 对文章中实时互动的模拟器感到惊叹，尤其是可以模拟不同操作并追踪用户行为。
  - cadamsdotcom: 赞赏作者对网页和Mac的热爱，认为这是对技术力量的致敬。
  - rezmason: 对模拟器内事件的实现方式感到好奇，并探讨了像素分析的技术细节。

• [对设备识别问题的讨论]
  - dmitshur: 对文章中提到“在电脑上打开”感到困惑，因为他的Surface Pro X被识别为非电脑，后来作者添加了额外说明以解决此问题。

• [怀旧情感]

  - jfvinueza: 回忆起PowerBook G4，并对文章和网站表示赞赏。
  - vintagedave: 怀念早期Mac OS的控制面板设计，认为现在的系统设置缺乏关怀和个性。

• [对现代系统设置的批评]
  - kamel3d: 批评MacOS Ventura的设置界面布局混乱，难以找到所需选项。

• [设备兼容性问题]

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到对文章和技术实现的赞赏，尤其是实时模拟和怀旧元素的结合。
- 对现代系统设置的批评集中在用户体验和界面设计的变化上。
- 设备识别和兼容性问题引发了一些技术讨论，特别是不同设备和浏览器的识别机制。
- 用户习惯的延续也反映出对界面设计变化的适应问题。

44505171.article_content:
Frame of preference
A history of Mac settings, 1984â2004
As a designer, Iâm meant to dislike settings. As a user, I love them.
Every year I celebrate Settings Day: a day when I take a look at the options and toggles in all the apps I use. I do this out of curiosity â what was added since the last time I looked? â but also because I love this way of getting to know software: peeking under the hood, walking the back alleys, learning what has been tricky or important enough to be equipped with a checkbox.
During the last Settings Day, I had a realization that the totemic 1984 Mac control panel, designed by Susan Kare, is still to this day perhaps the only settings screen ever brought up in casual conversation.
I kept wondering about that screen, and about what happened since then. Turns out, the Mac settings have lived a far more fascinating life than I imagined, have been redesigned many times, and can tell us a lot about the early history and the troubled upbringing of this interesting machine.
Join me on a journey through the first twenty years of Macâs control panels.
1984
Itâs rare when software matches hardware so well.
Even already in 1979, the Macintosh was envisioned as a home appliance akin to a toaster or a TV. This was documented in
one of my favorite memos of all time
. Get the machine out of the box. Leave the screwdriver in the drawer. There is no step three.
Once you do that,
open the Apple menu
, and then
launch the Control Panel
, and you will find a small appliance hiding inside the machine, too. A European appliance, even âÂ outside of the title bar, there are absolutely no words present here.
The Control Panel is a handsome and tight design, put together by Susan Kare as the
last desk accessory
, just weeks before the Macâs announcement. It feels alive, depicting a perhaps surprising amount of movement sometimes via animation, sometimes via comic book-inspired conventions: soundwaves exiting the speaker, menus blinking upon activation, a finger pressing a key, the mouse rolling on the desk. Itâs also a playground of sorts for early GUI experiments: there is an early
slider
here, some
steppers
for date and time, a custom cursor, and a mini map showing a miniature desktop.
The last two are in service of the most contentious addition:
customizing the desktop pattern
. The original Mac team was divided on this one, worrying this would lead to âabominable patternsâ and therefore âugly desktopsâ â an ongoing design challenge for any setting that is not about how something works, but about how something
looks
.
Future, more garish desktop options on computers and eventually smartphones would render these early reservations quaint. This might be the best that the Mac desktop will look for about the next twenty years. But at this moment, it felt serious. The creator of
MacPaint
rebelled and built his app so that any custom background would be drawn over by a default 50% checkerboard anyway. But can you even make an ugly desktop pattern with just 64 black pixels to mess with? Maybeâ¦ The most surprising is the fact that the team also prepared 41 beautiful built-in patterns, but hid them inside this control panel with the only hints how to get them appearing in the manual.
At this point in time, this was the only way you could truly customize your Mac to fit your personality, and itâs nice that it also happens to be one thatâs fun to use, ironically perhaps inspired by MacPaint and its
FatBits
setting.
Other controls might be slightly surprising: out of just ten settings, three are dedicated to motor memory. The two keyboard toggles make sense. Even in the early 1980s, there were keyboards â terminals or electric typewriters â whose repeating style you might have gotten used to. We already knew that once something lodges itself in your fingertips, itâs really hard to override it, even consciously, so it was clever to add customization to work around that.
But the third option is for double clicking that never existed before. There werenât really decades or even years of studies done on mouse usage, either. I imagine the creators felt it was better safe than sorry.
This early Control Panel has been celebrated since, even though there are mistakes here: the inconsistent Chicago 3, the top section being one pixel too short, and an occasional uneven border. The UI, like the whole Mac, is slow and clunky â you can see the panel, the windows, even the menus struggling to be drawn with required haste. (Only the mouse pointer is speedy, and it was
a small miracle
how it got this way.)
For people using this early Mac, this was likely frustrating as hell. Today, it feels like a perfect intro for a new little machine, the best dense collection of pixels this side of
Winamp
. Itâs cute, it gets the job done, and it has tons of charm.
Control Panel embroidery
Stitched and patterned by
gmatom
1986
Two years later, and a lot of that charm is gone. Susan Kare and Steve Jo

data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: libpostal是一个开源的C语言库，用于解析和标准化全球街道地址。它利用统计自然语言处理（NLP）和开放地理数据，目标是理解各种语言的地址格式。该库可以将人类使用的非结构化地址转换为规范形式，便于机器对比和全文索引，特别适用于地图、交通、快递等应用。虽然libpostal本身不是完整的地理编码器，但可以作为预处理步骤，提高国际化地址处理的智能性和一致性。该项目支持Python、Ruby、Go、Java、PHP和NodeJS等多种语言绑定，并提供了详细的安装指南。公司和个人可以通过赞助或捐赠支持该项目的持续发展。

争议焦点：
• 地址解析和规范化的可行性及其实际效果，特别是在面对非标准化地址时。

libpostal: international street address NLP
libpostal is a C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world using statistical NLP and open data. The goal of this project is to understand location-based strings in every language, everywhere. For a more comprehensive overview of the research behind libpostal, be sure to check out the (lengthy) introductory blog posts:
Original post
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap
Follow-up for 1.0 release
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap: Part 2

Addresses and the locations they represent are essential for any application dealing with maps (place search, transportation, on-demand/delivery services, check-ins, reviews). Yet even the simplest addresses are packed with local conventions, abbreviations and context, making them difficult to index/query effectively with traditional full-text search engines. This library helps convert the free-form addresses that humans use into clean normalized forms suitable for machine comparison and full-text indexing. Though libpostal is not itself a full geocoder, it can be used as a preprocessing step to make any geocoding application smarter, simpler, and more consistent internationally.

The core library is written in pure C. Language bindings for
Python
,
Ruby
,
Go
,

,
PHP

NodeJS
are officially supported and it's easy to write bindings in other languages.
Sponsors
If your company is using libpostal, consider asking your organization to sponsor the project. Interpreting what humans mean when they refer to locations is far from a solved problem, and sponsorships help us pursue new frontiers in geospatial NLP. As a sponsor, your company logo will appear prominently on the Github repo page along with a link to your site.
Sponsorship info
Backers
Individual users can also help support open geo NLP research by making a monthly donation:
Installation (Mac/Linux)
Before you install, make sure you have the following prerequisites:
On Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y curl build-essential autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
On CentOS/RHEL
sudo yum install curl autoconf automake libtool pkgconfig
On macOS
Install with one command via
MacPorts
:
port install libpostal
Or as follows with
Homebrew
:
brew install curl autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
Then to install the C library:
If you're using an M1 Mac, add
--disable-sse2
to the
./configure
command. This will result in poorer performance but the build will succeed.
git clone https://github.com/openvenues/libpostal
cd libpostal
# skip if installing for the first time
make distclean
./bootstrap.sh
# omit --datadir flag to install data in current directory
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
make -j4
# For Intel/AMD processors and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
# For Apple / ARM cpus and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] --disable-sse2
# For the improved Senzing model:
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] MODEL=senzing
make -j8
sudo make install
# On Linux it's probably a good idea to run
sudo ldconfig
libpostal has support for pkg-config, so you can use the pkg-config to print the flags needed to link your program against it:
pkg-config --cflags libpostal         # print compiler flags
pkg-config --libs libpostal           # print linker flags
pkg-config --cflags --l

data.title: Choosing a Database Schema for Polymorphic Data (2024)
data.author: gm678
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在关系型数据库中设计模式时面临的挑战，尤其是处理多态数据（polymorphic data）的困难。多态数据是指可以有多种不同形态的数据类型。文章以患者支付信息为例，说明了如何在SQL中建模这种数据。文章介绍了一种简单的方案——使用具有可空字段的单表模式，即“单表继承”或“层次表”，但这种方法存在一些问题，如难以验证数据的不变性、错误信息不明确以及未来扩展性差。此外，随着数据集的增大，这种设计可能导致性能问题。文章还提到，尽管可以对表添加约束来解决部分问题，但这些约束会变得复杂且难以维护。最终，这种方案需要在数据完整性、可扩展性和性能之间做出权衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在处理数据库中的多态数据和复杂数据结构时，不同技术的优缺点和选择。

不同观点：
• reaanb2 认为SQL中的检查约束和存储过程可以提供更好的错误信息和事务管理。他建议结合使用存储过程与特定数据库设计（如主键和唯一键）来处理多态数据，并提到SQL在处理外键约束和排除约束方面的不足。
• bob1029 讨论了JSON作为blob列的优缺点，指出在某些情况下（如使用快速序列化器时），JSON blob可以很好地工作，但当需要跨JSON属性进行连接时，JSON可能不是最佳选择。
• gm678 引用了Martin Fowler的企业应用架构模式，如单表继承、类表继承和具体表继承，认为这些模式可以应用于当前讨论的问题。
• 1st1 提到Gel语言中对多态模式和查询的支持，认为这是处理多态数据的一种简便方法。
• fmjrey 认为传统的OO和RDBMS方法在处理现代分布式系统时已达到其极限，提出了EAV数据库（如Datomic、XTDB）和Rama等新方法，作为减少复杂性和提高扩展性的解决方案。
• hot_gril 反对将类型存储为数据库列，倾向于使用可空列或JSON来处理多态数据，具体选择取决于是否需要对字段进行连接操作。
• acquiesce 认为下游代码经常需要处理多态性破坏的情况，主张多态应仅用于行为而非数据，并建议在特定情况下才使用子类化。
• feitico 简单直接地推荐使用NoSQL，特别是MongoDB，来处理多态数据。
• j45 质疑为何不直接使用多态数据库来处理多态数据，认为关系型数据库在处理此类数据时可能过于复杂。
• toolslive 提出了列存储作为另一种处理方法的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到对不同数据库设计模式（如单表继承、类表继承、具体表继承）的引用和链接，提供了进一步阅读的资源。
• 有人提出使用NoSQL作为替代方案，而另一些人则在关系型数据库的框架内寻找解决方案。
• 对多态数据的处理存在争议，特别是在如何在数据库中表示和查询多态数据方面，存在不同的看法和实践建议。
• 讨论中还涉及了EAV模型和Rama等新兴技术和方法，作为处理复杂数据和分布式系统的新思路。

Designing a schema for your relational database is a daunting task that has long term implications for the database's performance, maintainability, and correctness. And it often requires making decisions before having a clear picture of the exact shape and distribution of your data, or what the common access patterns will look like. It's not a permanent decision: tables can be altered and databases migrated. But these migrations can be slow and expensive.
To top it all off, some data is less amenable to relational modeling than others.
Polymorphic Data
, in particular, is a common occurrence that is difficult to model in SQL. You've probably worked with polymorphic data before, even if you're not familiar with the term.
Example: Patient Payment Info
Imagine you're a medical provider storing patient payment methods. Every patient is either insured or uninsured, and you need to store different data for each patient based on their insurance status.
If you've written code in a functional language, you might be familiar with algebraic data types. For instance, you could represent this schema in Haskell with the following ADT:
type
Provider
=
String
type
MemberId
=
Int
type
CardNumber
=
String
type
BillingAddress
=
String
data
PaymentInfo
=
Insured
Provider
MemberId
|
Uninsured
CardNumber
BillingAddress
If you're more accustomed to object oriented programming, you might implement this same data type via abstract classes and inheritance, like the following Java code:
abstract
class
PaymentInfo
{
}
class

String
provider
;
int
memberId
;
}
class
Uninsured
extends
PaymentInfo
{
String
cardNumber
;
String
billingAddress
;
}
These are both examples of polymorphic data: a datatype where the data can take multiple different shapes. The word comes from Greek roots: "poly" meaning many, and "morph" meaning form. So, data that can take many forms. When a relational database needs to model polymorphic data, we typically use the term
polymorphic association
instead.
Sometimes, like in the above example, a polymorphic association is the best way to model your data type. But there's no obvious way to represent this data in a relational database. If you want to include data like this in your database, you're going to have to make some tradeoffs.
Let's look at some different schemas that attempt to model this data. We're going to use MySQL as our chosen dialect here, but the process is similar regardless of dialect.
Approach 1 - Single Table With Nullable Fields
The simplest schema would be one that has a single table, with a field for each value that
may
appear in a record, or may be
NULL
. Such a schema would look like this:
CREATE
TABLE
patients
(
id
INT
PRIMARY
KEY
,
insurance_provider
TEXT
,
insurance_member_id
INT
,
card_number
TEXT
,
billing_address
TEXT
)
;
In each row, we set
insurance_provider
and
insurance_member_id
if the patient is insured, and
card_number
and
billing_address
if the patient is uninsured. The unused fields get set to
NULL
.
This technique is sometimes also called "Single Table Inheritance" or "Table-Per-Hierarchy", because a single table is used to represent an entire hierarchy of types.
This works, but it has several problems. Mainly, our data has several invariants that the database cannot easily validate. Among them:
In a single row, the fields for insured and uninsured patients should not both be set to non-NULL values.
We would like to enforce that
insurance_member_id
cannot be NULL for insured patients, but we can't add a
NOT NULL
constraint on the column, because it also
must
be
NULL
for uninsured patients.
We can add constraints to the table, but they're pretty obtuse, and the error messages if the constraints get violated are opaque:
CREATE
TABLE
patients
(
id
INT
PRIMARY
KEY
,
insurance_provider
TEXT
,
insurance_member_id
INT
,
card_number
TEXT
,
billing_address
TEXT
,
CHECK
(
(
insurance_provider
IS
NULL
)
=
(
insurance_member_id
IS
NULL
)
)
,
CHECK
(
(
card_number
IS
NULL
)
=
(
billing_address
IS
NULL
)
)
,
CHECK
(
(
insurance_provider
IS
NULL
)
+
(
card_number
IS
NULL
)
=
1
)
)
;
This will result in an error if we attempt to insert a patient record with neither payment type or both payment types, but the error message isn't very helpful:
>
INSERT
INTO
patients
(
id
,
insurance_provider
,
insurance_member_id
)
VALUES
(
1
,
"OneMedical"
,
NULL
)
;
ERROR
3819
(
HY000
)
at line
1
:
Check
constraint
'patients_chk_1'
is
violated
.
These checks would only grow in complexity as the number of fields in each payment method grows. And what if we later want to add a third type of payment info? We'd have to add additional columns to the table, modifying every existing row and changing the table schema.
There's another, more subtle issue happening here: performance. A schema like this is fast for small datasets because storing all the records in a single table allows the engine to perform fewer joins. But as the size of the dataset grows, this table could become a bot
44505165.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在关系型数据库中设计模式时面临的挑战，尤其是处理多态数据（polymorphic data）的困难。多态数据是指可以有多种不同形态的数据类型。文章以患者支付信息为例，说明了如何在SQL中建模这种数据。文章介绍了一种简单的方案——使用具有可空字段的单表模式，即“单表继承”或“层次表”，但这种方法存在一些问题，如难以验证数据的不变性、错误信息不明确以及未来扩展性差。此外，随着数据集的增大，这种设计可能导致性能问题。文章还提到，尽管可以对表添加约束来解决部分问题，但这些约束会变得复杂且难以维护。最终，这种方案需要在数据完整性、可扩展性和性能之间做出权衡。

data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了C语言中如何将数据与函数调用配对的历史演变，重点介绍了`qsort`函数的局限性及后续解决方案。最初，`qsort`只接受一个函数指针，无法传递额外数据，导致开发者需要使用`static`变量或全局变量来实现自定义行为。这带来了数据共享和多线程问题，且被视为不良代码质量的标志。为解决此问题，GNU引入了嵌套函数（Nested Functions），允许函数定义在局部作用域并访问本地数据，避免了全局变量的使用。嵌套函数提供了更直观和安全的解决方案，但其安全性在当时并未被深入理解。文章最后提到嵌套函数的优势包括外观和行为类似常规函数，能访问本地数据，且只需一个函数指针。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言中嵌套函数、可执行栈问题以及C语言的局限性与替代方案

不同观点：
• [uecker的观点]  
  - 认为将GNU嵌套函数加入ISO C标准的提案已经明确指出了可执行栈的问题，并提出了替代实现方式（如引入新的函数类型）。  
  - 不同意将非可执行栈直接视为漏洞的原因，认为这是一种缓解技术，尽管返回导向编程（ROP）可以绕过这种保护，但这种技术仍然很重要。

• [rurban的观点]  
  - 提到C语言中关于函数与数据结合的早期尝试，例如Bruno Haible的回调库（libffcall），这实际上是编译器领域称为闭包的早期实现。

• [pjmlp的观点]  
  - 认为类似功能应通过Objective-C或C++等语言实现，而不是扩展C语言。  
  - 主张接受C语言的局限性，将其视为类似于可移植汇编的语言，承认其安全缺陷，并建议在需要更高抽象和安全性时选择其他语言。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于C语言是否应该扩展以支持嵌套函数或其他高级特性，还是应该保持其低级特性并依赖其他语言提供更高级的抽象和安全机制。  
- uecker强调了非可执行栈作为缓解技术的重要性，但承认其局限性。  
- rurban提供了有关C语言早期尝试的历史背景，指出了闭包概念的早期实现。  
- pjmlp则主张放弃对C语言的这种扩展，建议使用其他更适合的语言来实现这些功能。

Concerns and problems around sharing data only grew in time as each program had to manage larger and larger swaths of 1980’s-style global variable soups, something that has famously ended up being used as a sign of negative code quality in legal matters. data.title: Where can I see Hokusai's Great Wave today?
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary:
目前，葛饰北斋的著名作品《神奈川冲浪里》可以在以下地点观看：

- 🇮🇹 特雷维索的Musei Civici，展出至2025年9月28日。
- 🇫🇷 南特的Musée d’histoire，展出至2025年9月7日。

此外，该作品还可在以下地点看到：

- 🇮🇹 的里雅斯特东方艺术博物馆（Civic Museum of Oriental Art, Trieste）
- 🇮🇹 维罗纳的Palazzo Maffei Casa Museo
- 🇺🇸 法明顿的Hill-Stead Museum

另有55个地点也可能会展出该作品。了解更多信息或将博物馆/画廊列入展示列表，可访问相关网站或GitHub页面。

data.title: Phrase origin: Why do we "call" functions?
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了编程术语中为何使用“调用”（call）函数的说法。作者通过几个类比解释了这个术语的来源，包括将函数调用比作召唤朋友或仆人，以及像打电话一样请求帮助。文章指出，函数“调用”更接近于“召唤”子程序的概念，源自从图书馆中“调用”书籍的术语。文章追溯了“调用号”（call number）在图书馆学中的使用历史，并引用了John W. Mauchly在1947年的文章，该文章讨论了计算机子程序库中的“调用”概念。MANIAC II的1956年手册进一步明确了这一术语，描述了如何通过“调用号”从子程序库中召唤子程序用于程序组装。这表明编程中的“调用”函数术语源自图书馆学的“调用”书籍概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于计算机术语"call"（调用）的起源和使用的讨论，以及与其他相关术语和语言现象的比较。

不同观点：
• jamesemmott引用Grace Hopper的观点，认为"compiler"一词源于从图书馆的"call number"（索书号）中获得灵感，子程序的调用（call）也与从图书馆中提取资料有关。
• seanc认为图书馆学对现代计算的贡献被低估，比如通过卡片目录解释数据库索引。
• Swiffy0分享了芬兰语中"call"的翻译为"kutsua"，意为"邀请"或"召唤"，指出在不同语言中该词的含义差异。
• fanf2提供了1951年Wilkes, Wheeler, Gill著作中的例子，显示"call in"用于调用子程序，并提供了相关文献资源。
• userbinator提到除了"call"以外，还会使用"invoke"或"execute"，并对ESL（英语作为第二语言）计算机科学学生误用"call"表示不满。
• skaushik92反思了"library"一词的起源，认识到其最初指的是磁带等物理存储介质。
• gorgoiler提到舞蹈中"call"的用法，认为与函数调用无关，但描述了每一步的算法。
• ks2478引用了音乐中的"call and response"现象，甚至提到返回值的概念。
• Ferret7446通过观察提出，新词的传播依赖于其易记和能引起共鸣的特性，并以"salty"为例说明这一过程。
• walthamstow离题地提到视频通话中使用的"jump on a call"这一表达。
• pixelpoet提到游戏中"proc"的用法，推测其来源于程序调用（procedure call）。
• kragen讨论了其他可能的动词如"instantiating"、"evaluating"、"computing"等，并引用了Mauchly的文献，指出早期文献中使用了"utilize"和"direct"等词。
• vincent-manis引用莎士比亚的《亨利四世》台词，幽默地说明调用（call）与响应的关系。
• amelius幽默地提到使用"gosub"（go to subroutine）来调用函数。
• seabass表达了对计算机历史讨论的喜爱，并好奇为何使用"throw"和"raise"来描述错误处理，以及为何"for"被用于循环结构。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多个语言和文化背景下的术语使用差异，比如芬兰语中的"kutsua"。
• 提到了多个与"call"类似的动词和术语，如"invoke"、"execute"、"jump"等，展示了计算机术语的多样性和历史演变。
• 讨论中涉及了多个历史文献和具体例子，如Grace Hopper的言论、早期编程书籍等，提供了丰富的背景资料。
• 有些评论带有幽默和个人观察，如引用莎士比亚台词和"salty"一词的类比。
• 最后，seabass提出了对其他计算机术语如"throw"、"raise"和循环结构中"for"使用的思考，扩展了讨论的范围。

44506251.article_content:
Phrase origin: Why do we “call” functions?
On
StackExchange
,
someone asks why programmers talk about “calling” a function. Several possible allusions spring to mind:
Calling a function is like calling on a friend — we go, we stay a while, we come back.
Calling a function is like calling for a servant — a summoning to perform a task.
Calling a function is like making a phone call — we ask a question and get an answer from outside ourselves.
The true answer seems to be the middle one — “calling” as in “calling up, summoning” —
but indirectly, originating in the notion of “calling for” a subroutine out of a library of subroutines
in the same way that we’d “call for” a book out of a closed-stack library of books.
The OED’s first citation for
call number
in the library-science sense comes from
Melvil Dewey
(yes,
that Dewey
)
in 1876. The OED defines it as:
A mark, esp. a number, on a library book, or listed in a library’s catalogue,
indicating the book’s location in the library; a book’s press mark or
shelf mark
.
I see librarians using the term “call-number” in
The Library Journal
13
.9
(1888) as if it was very well established already by that point:
Mr. Davidson read a letter from Mr. A.W. Tyler […] enclosing sample of the new
call blank
used at the
Plainfield (N.J.) P. L., giving more room for the signature and address of the applicant. […]
“In connection with Mr. Tyler’s new
call slip
[…] I always feel outraged when I make up a long list
of
call numbers
in order to make sure of a book, and then the librarian keeps the list, and the next
time I have it all to do over again.”
According to
The Organization of Information
4th ed. (Joudrey & Taylor, 2017):
Call number.
A notation on a resource that matches the same notation in the metadata description and
is used to identify and locate the item; it often consists of a classification notation and a cutter number,
and it may also include a workmark and/or a date. It is the number used to “call” for an item in a closed-stack
library; thus the source of the name “call number.”
Cutter number.
A designation with the purpose of alphabetizing all works that have exactly the same classification notation.
Named for
Charles Ammi Cutter
, who devised such a scheme, but spelled
with a small
c
when referring to another such table that is not Cutter’s own.
John W. Mauchly’s article
“Preparation of problems for EDVAC-type machines”
(1947)
uses the English word “call” only twice, yet this seems to be an important early attestation of the word
in the context of a “library” of computer subroutines:
Important questions for the users of a machine are: How easily can reference be made to any of the subroutines?
How hard is it to initiate a subroutine? What conditions can be used to terminate a subroutine? And with what
facility can control revert to any part of the original sequence or some further sequence […] Facilities
for conditional and other transfers to subroutines, transfers to still further subroutines, and transfers
back again, are certain to be used frequently.
[…] the position in the memory at which arguments are placed can be standardized, so that whenever a subroutine
is
called in
to perform a calculation, the subroutine will automatically know that the argument which is to
be used is at a specified place.
[…] Some of them might be written out in a handbook and transferred to the coding of the problem as needed,
but those of any complexity presumably ought to be in a
library
— that is, a set of magnetic tapes in which
previously coded problems of permanent value are stored.
[…] One of the problems which must be met in this case is the method of withdrawal from the library
and of compilation in the proper sequence for the particular problem. […] It is possible […] to evolve
a coding instruction for placing the subroutines in the memory at places known to the machine, and in such
a way that they may easily be
called into use
[…] all one needs to do is make brief reference to them
by number, as they are indicated in the coding.
The manual for the
“MANIAC II assembly routine”
(January 1956)
follows Mauchly’s sketch pretty closely. MANIAC II has a paper-tape “library” of subroutines which
can be summoned up (by the assembler) to become part of a fully assembled program, and in fact each item
in the “library” has an identifying “call number,” just like every book in a real library has a call number:
The assembly routine for Maniac II is designed to translate descriptive code into absolute code. […]
The bulk of the descriptive tape consists of a series of instructions, separated, by control words,
into numbered groups called
boxes
[because flowcharts: today we’d say “basic blocks”]. The allowed
box numbers are
01
through
EF
[. …] If the address [in an instruction’s address field] is
FXXX
,
then the instruction must be a transfer, and the transfer is to the subroutine whose
call number
is
XXX
. The most common subroutines are on the same magnetic tape as the assembly routine, a

data.author: sabman
data.article_summary: EarthGPT是一个利用大型语言模型（LLMs）和现代遥感技术处理多光谱卫星影像的平台。用户可以通过其演示功能体验卫星图像分析，并能通过hi@earthgpt.app联系平台。该平台由Geobase提供支持，旨在提供先进的地球观测数据分析服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将大型语言模型（LLM）应用于遥感图像分析的工具、技术及其潜在价值展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **notachatbot123**：对使用"turbo"色彩映射表示质疑，认为应该考虑色彩科学的长期研究，引用了经典的色彩研究资源，暗示色彩选择可能不够科学。
• **goroutines**：对将LLM应用于遥感分析表示支持，认为像Planet、Descartes等公司也应该朝这个方向发展。
• **joshvm**：提到遥感领域的范围正在扩大，并提供了一个包含基础模型和LLM集成的资源列表，指出该领域的工具和资源越来越丰富。
• **jesterx**：提到另一个使用LLM生成Google Earth Engine代码的论文，提供了一个相关项目（SatGPT）的链接，暗示这种方法并非全新。
• **rubyfan**：质疑LLM在此应用中的独特价值，询问如果没有LLM，哪些任务会更难完成，或者LLM带来了哪些新的能力。
• **RamblingCTO**：对整体想法表示赞赏，但指出在实际使用中遇到的问题，如无法查看某些示例，建议提供更多预定义的示例供用户参考。
• **sabman**：分享了个人经验，表示在多年从事遥感分析产品开发后，认识到LLM在分析影像和光谱带方面的潜力，支持将LLM引入该领域。
• **mahmed315**：简单表示这是一个好主意，没有深入讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：主要集中在LLM在遥感分析中的实际价值和应用效果。rubyfan对LLM的必要性提出质疑，而sabman和goroutines等人则表示支持。
• 实用性问题：RamblingCTO提到了工具在实际使用中的可用性问题，强调了用户体验的重要性。
• 资源分享：joshvm提供了相关资源列表，为感兴趣的用户提供了更多信息来源。
• 对比与参考：jesterx提到了类似的项目（SatGPT），为讨论提供了一个对比的参考点。

这些观点共同构成了对LLM在遥感分析中应用的多角度讨论，涵盖了技术、实用性和科学性等方面。

44488742.article_summary: EarthGPT是一个利用大型语言模型（LLMs）和现代遥感技术处理多光谱卫星影像的平台。用户可以通过其演示功能体验卫星图像分析，并能通过hi@earthgpt.app联系平台。该平台由Geobase提供支持，旨在提供先进的地球观测数据分析服务。
44488742.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将大型语言模型（LLM）应用于遥感图像分析的工具、技术及其潜在价值展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **notachatbot123**：对使用"turbo"色彩映射表示质疑，认为应该考虑色彩科学的长期研究，引用了经典的色彩研究资源，暗示色彩选择可能不够科学。
• **goroutines**：对将LLM应用于遥感分析表示支持，认为像Planet、Descartes等公司也应该朝这个方向发展。
• **joshvm**：提到遥感领域的范围正在扩大，并提供了一个包含基础模型和LLM集成的资源列表，指出该领域的工具和资源越来越丰富。
• **jesterx**：提到另一个使用LLM生成Google Earth Engine代码的论文，提供了一个相关项目（SatGPT）的链接，暗示这种方法并非全新。
• **rubyfan**：质疑LLM在此应用中的独特价值，询问如果没有LLM，哪些任务会更难完成，或者LLM带来了哪些新的能力。
• **RamblingCTO**：对整体想法表示赞赏，但指出在实际使用中遇到的问题，如无法查看某些示例，建议提供更多预定义的示例供用户参考。
• **sabman**：分享了个人经验，表示在多年从事遥感分析产品开发后，认识到LLM在分析影像和光谱带方面的潜力，支持将LLM引入该领域。
• **mahmed315**：简单表示这是一个好主意，没有深入讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：主要集中在LLM在遥感分析中的实际价值和应用效果。rubyfan对LLM的必要性提出质疑，而sabman和goroutines等人则表示支持。
• 实用性问题：RamblingCTO提到了工具在实际使用中的可用性问题，强调了用户体验的重要性。
• 资源分享：joshvm提供了相关资源列表，为感兴趣的用户提供了更多信息来源。
• 对比与参考：jesterx提到了类似的项目（SatGPT），为讨论提供了一个对比的参考点。

这些观点共同构成了对LLM在遥感分析中应用的多角度讨论，涵盖了技术、实用性和科学性等方面。

data.author: AntonioBarthes
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI与社会语言学中的权力 dynamics 以及在使用AI生成内容进行学术讨论时的严谨性

不同观点：
• **tony_borlini** 认为AI（DeepSeek-V3）不仅能够总结文章观点，还能进行反驳，这让人感到惊讶。他通过让AI生成博客回应了一篇关于AI、权力与社会语言学的文章，并将该回应发布在个人博客上，邀请读者进一步讨论。

• **carschno** 提供了一个与讨论相关的学术文章的永久链接，指向一篇可能与AI和社会语言学相关的学术资源，但并未直接发表个人观点，而是提供了一个供进一步研究的参考。

• **whatevsmate** 持批评态度，认为社会语言学家在讨论AI和权力 dynamics 时应更加严谨，而不应仅仅基于与一个AI的互动就做出广泛结论。他质疑了所使用的AI模型和版本的透明性，并讽刺这种研究方法为“自我民族志研究”和“ cynical fart-sniffing ”。

• **joules77** 则从人类认知局限性的角度出发，认为“幻觉”和“胡说八道”是人类认知的自然部分，因为人类大脑无法容纳所有知识。他将这种现象与人类在面对知识不足时的默认行为联系起来，并以“本地黑猩猩首领”的比喻来强调这一点。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**在于使用AI生成内容进行学术讨论的严谨性和透明性。whatevsmate对研究方法和AI模型的选择提出了质疑，认为不应轻率地根据AI生成的内容做出广泛结论。
• **讨论的另一层面**是AI在互动中表现出“反驳”能力是否值得惊讶，以及这种能力对学术讨论的实际价值。tony_borlini对此感到惊讶并认为值得进一步探讨，而whatevsmate则持怀疑态度。
• **joules77** 的评论引入了一种人类认知与AI行为之间的类比，为讨论提供了一个新视角，即AI的“幻觉”和“胡说八道”是否可以与人类的类似行为相提并论。

data.title: Is the doc bot docs, or not?
data.author: tobr
data.article_summary: 在这篇文章中，Robin Sloan描述了他在升级Shopify电子邮件通知模板时，使用Shopify的LLM开发文档机器人获取帮助的经历。他询问如何检测订单是否包含通过Shopify Collective履行的商品，文档机器人提供了代码，但实际应用中发现该代码无效，原因是订单标签在确认邮件生成时尚未存在。Robin反思文档机器人的价值，认为提供错误信息可能比没有帮助更糟糕，质疑这种工具是否真正有助于文档工作。他最终提供了一个有效的代码解决方案，并表达了对文档准确性的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文档机器人（Docs bots）在实际应用中的挑战和表现

不同观点：
• **Emil_Sorensen**：认为文档机器人很难在生产环境中做到完美。需要在依赖底层文档和利用LLM潜在知识之间取得平衡，而这需要大量的评估（evals）。特别是在处理GraphQL schema时，难度更大。同时提到其公司Kapa.ai在为多家企业开发文档助手。
• **Cco**：其公司经过多次评估后，发现当前的LLM机器人尚未达到可以向客户提供的标准，约有60%的答案是好的，20%是中立或差的，20%是有害的。目前最好的方法仍是将文档添加到本地LLM IDE中自行查询。
• **Dworks**：预测未来因非确定性系统导致的问题会引发AI泡沫破裂。认为当前公司不顾系统非确定性问题，强行使用AI将导致严重后果。
• **Schnable**：提到其使用Gemini时遇到系统编造不支持的功能和代码的情况，认为当前AI在产品中的使用尚未成熟。
• **Shlomo_Z**：对Shopify的文档机器人提出质疑，建议创建免费测试项以免去使用信用卡交易的必要。
• **Bewelge**：认为Shopify的帮助页面像“销售文档”，不提供实际操作指导。其曾遇到文档机器人无法正确回答技术问题的情况，但在更新后情况有所改善。
• **Simonw**：希望文档机器人能正确回答复杂技术问题，并建议建立一个能测试代码的环境以提高答案的可靠性。
• **Bravesoul2**：质疑Shopify需要真实信用卡测试的做法，认为不如Stripe的测试机制。
• **Ngriffiths**：认为文档机器人相当于读过文档的人，可能提供不同准确度的答案。直接引用文档是最好的方式，能确保责任明确。
• **Schaum**：提到Gurubase.io，可以用来与文档交互并验证响应。
• **Trjordan**：指出文档和文档机器人都有错误率，文档可能有遗漏或误导，而文档机器人速度更快。认为在测试代码后再投入生产是合理的折中。
• **Domk**：认为对Shopify等平台的深入理解是避免错误的关键，AI仅依赖文档是不够的。
• **Ysofunny**：将文档比作有损压缩的JPEG，查询越具体，噪声越大。
• **Goroutines**：建议使用精确的逐步文档（如install.md）配合简单的RAG系统和编码代理，认为这是正确的方向。
• **Anentropic**：猜测窄领域的文档机器人表现不如ChatGPT等在“搜索”模式下的表现。

补充讨论：
• 文档机器人在生产环境中的表现和可靠性是主要关注点，特别是在处理技术文档和复杂查询时。
• 不同用户和公司对文档机器人的期望和实际体验存在差异，有的认为其速度快但准确性不足，有的则希望其能提供更可靠的技术指导。
• 争议的焦点在于文档机器人的错误率和其是否能替代传统文档或人类经验，以及如何在速度和准确性之间取得平衡。

44507244.article_content:
This is a post from Robin Sloan ’s lab blog & notebook. You can visit the blog’s homepage , or learn more about me . Is the doc bot docs, or not? July 8, 2025 Upgrading my Shopify email noti­fi­ca­tion templates this morning, I asked Shopifyâs LLM-powered devel­oper doc­u­men­ta­tion bot this ques­tion: Whatâs the syntax, in Liquid, to detect whether an order in an email noti­fi­ca­tion con­tains items that will be ful­filled through Shopify Collective? Iâd done a few tra­di­tional searches, but couldnât find an answer, so I thought, okay, letâs try the doc bot! The reply came, quick and clean: {% if order.tags contains 'Shopify Collective' %}

Some items in your order are being fulfilled by a partner merchant through Shopify Collective.

{% endif %} Looks great. I added this code, but it didnât work; the con­di­tion wasnât being satisfied, even when orders had the nec­es­sary tag, vis­ible on the admin screen. Shopify doesnât pro­vide a way to test uncon­ven­tional email for­mats without actu­ally placing real orders, so I did my cus­tomary dance of order-refund, order-refund, order-refund. My credit card is going to get locked one of these days. Turns out, the Shopify Collective tag isnât present on the order at the time the con­fir­ma­tion email is generated. Itâs added later, pos­sibly just moments later, by some other cryptic Shopify process. I donât think this is doc­u­mented anywhere, so in that sense, itâs not sur­prising the doc­u­men­ta­tion bot got it wrong. My ques­tion is: whatâs the point of a doc bot that just takes a guess? More point­edly: is the doc bot docs, or not? And very point­edly indeed: what are we even doing here?? Iâve sent other queries to the doc bot and received helpful replies; Iâd cat­e­go­rize these basi­cally as search: âHow do I do X?â âWhatâs the syntax for Y?â But I believe this is a sit­u­a­tion in which the cost of bad advice out­weighs the ben­efit of quick help by 10X, at least. I can, in fact, figure out how to do X using the real docs. Only the doc bot can make things up. If it was Claude making this kind of mistake, Iâd be annoyed but not surprised. But this is Shopifyâs sanc­tioned helper! It waits twin­kling in the header of every page of the dev site. I suppose there are domains in which just taking a guess is okay; is the offi­cial doc­u­men­ta­tion one of them? I vote no, and I think a freestyling doc bot under­mines the effort and care of the folks at Shopify taking the time to write doc­u­men­ta­tion that is thor­ough and accurate. P.S. One working answer to my ques­tion looks like this: {% assign has_collective_item = false %} {% for line_item in line_items %} {% if line_item.product.tags contains 'Shopify Collective' %} {% assign has_collective_item = true %} {% endif %} {% endfor %} To the blog home page

data.author: doener

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：7-Zip软件的现状、功能、跨平台支持及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [d33] 认为7-Zip因缺乏zstd支持可能会失去竞争力，尤其在大文件处理上，zlib的性能不佳，而zlib-ng的改进效果有限。不过，他承认7-Zip在加密和文件分割方面表现出色。
• [avidiax] 质疑为什么Windows上的7-Zip有限制，而在Linux上没有发现类似问题。
• [fabiensanglard] 讨论了ZIP格式在写入磁盘前需要知道压缩大小的问题，猜测7-Zip可能是将压缩流缓存在RAM中，以保证输出的稳定性。
• [ninjis] 提到因为Windows现在原生支持7z格式，所以他不再觉得需要使用NanaZip。
• [aquir] 表示自从切换到macOS后，他一直怀念7-Zip软件。
• [leecarraher] 分享了他使用pbzip2的经验，认为尽管理论上压缩效率较低，但实际使用中没有显著差异。
• [izzydata] 提出了一个相关问题，询问"zip"术语是否与zip磁盘驱动器有相同的起源。
• [lihaciudaniel] 强调了7-Zip在移动设备上通过Termux和QEMU-utils处理虚拟磁盘文件的实用性。
• [ltbarcly3] 持批评态度，认为7-Zip在现代平台上已经不再重要，且其最新增强功能对绝大多数用户来说没有实际意义。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是7-Zip在现代计算环境中的相关性和实用性，尤其是在不同操作系统上的表现和限制。
• 另一个讨论点是关于压缩算法和格式的技术细节，例如压缩效率、写入机制以及缓存使用等。
• 还有对7-Zip跨平台支持的讨论，特别是macOS和Linux用户的需求和体验。
• 最后，评论中还包含了一些轻松或讽刺的言论，如[marcodiego]引用xkcd漫画，以及[ltbarcly3]对讨论本身的价值提出质疑。

• [fabiensanglard] 讨论了ZIP格式在写入磁盘前需要知道压缩大小的问题，猜测7-Zip可能是将压缩流缓存在RAM中，以保证输出的稳定性。
• [ninjis] 提到因为Windows现在原生支持7z格式，所以他不再觉得需要使用NanaZip。
• [aquir] 表示自从切换到macOS后，他一直怀念7-Zip软件。
• [leecarraher] 分享了他使用pbzip2的经验，认为尽管理论上压缩效率较低，但实际使用中没有显著差异。
• [izzydata] 提出了一个相关问题，询问"zip"术语是否与zip磁盘驱动器有相同的起源。
• [lihaciudaniel] 强调了7-Zip在移动设备上通过Termux和QEMU-utils处理虚拟磁盘文件的实用性。
• [ltbarcly3] 持批评态度，认为7-Zip在现代平台上已经不再重要，且其最新增强功能对绝大多数用户来说没有实际意义。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是7-Zip在现代计算环境中的相关性和实用性，尤其是在不同操作系统上的表现和限制。
• 另一个讨论点是关于压缩算法和格式的技术细节，例如压缩效率、写入机制以及缓存使用等。
• 还有对7-Zip跨平台支持的讨论，特别是macOS和Linux用户的需求和体验。
• 最后，评论中还包含了一些轻松或讽刺的言论，如[marcodiego]引用xkcd漫画，以及[ltbarcly3]对讨论本身的价值提出质疑。

data.title: SUSE launches new European digital sovereignty service to meet surging demand
data.author: saubeidl
data.article_summary: SUSE推出了一项名为"Sovereign Premium Support"的新服务，旨在帮助欧洲企业和政府在其IT基础设施中实现数字主权。该服务确保所有支持人员和数据都位于欧盟境内，客户支持数据存储在欧盟的网络和服务器上，且只有欧盟工作人员能访问敏感数据。此举响应了欧盟对数据隐私和独立性的日益关注，特别是面对非欧盟国家，尤其是美国公司的数据控制风险。SUSE的这项服务专为需要严格数据驻留和操作控制的组织设计，如国防、政府和执法部门，但也面向所有欧洲组织开放。这项服务在当前地缘政治不确定性增加的背景下，为欧洲客户提供了更强的安全保障和业务连续性支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕SUSE Linux、数据主权和欧洲数字主权的讨论

不同观点：
• [pjmlp] 认为FOSS（自由和开源软件）操作系统可能是摆脱美国主导的消费级操作系统及相关编程语言的唯一出路。他提到自己曾是Linux的狂热爱好者，对Linux发行版的碎片化以及桌面环境的梦想破灭感到失望，但特别指出SuSE和KDE的整合曾给他留下深刻印象。

• [jpalomaki] 强调仅仅关注服务器位置（如“存储在欧盟网络和服务器上”）并不足够，关键是谁在管理和控制这些服务器和网络。他认为讨论数据主权时，管理权比物理位置更重要。

• [0xfedcafe] 对SUSE在欧洲的被忽视表示不解，指出SUSE已经具备几乎所有必要的工具（如Rancher和openSUSE），并且在欧洲有相当的知名度。他对欧洲数字主权讨论中倾向于选择美国项目（如Fedora）而非SUSE表示质疑。

• [defraudbah] 对欧洲数据主权持怀疑态度，认为通过更多法规未必能赢得这场“战争”。他提到德国的先例，认为即使丹麦有可能迁移到Linux，最终可能也会像德国一样反复。同时，他对未来十年是否会有实质性改变表示悲观，预测只会出现更多补助和法律，但不会有根本性变化。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到SUSE的历史和其在欧洲的知名度，特别是其与KDE的整合及在开源项目中的地位。
• 数据主权的定义和实现方式存在争议，焦点在于服务器位置与管理权的相对重要性。
• 对欧洲是否能够真正实现数字主权存在不同看法，有人持乐观态度，认为SUSE是合适选择，而有人则持怀疑态度，认为法规和政策变化难以带来实际效果。

SUSE launches new European digital sovereignty support service to meet surging demand
With SUSE's help, European companies and governments can ensure their IT support, software, and data assets are safe.
Written by
Steven Vaughan-Nichols,
Senior Contributing Editor
Senior Contributing Editor
July 8, 2025 at 12:00 a.m. PT
Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images
Wary of the US government and tech companies, the European Union (EU) has seen a surge in support for
open source
and
Linux
. In the last few months, local EU governments,
including the city of Lyon in France,
the
German state of Schleswig-Holstein
, and
Denmark,
have begun their move to Linux and open-source software from
Microsoft Windows
and Office. Now, Luxembourg-based European open-source powerhouse
SUSE
is offering extensive support to businesses and governments that want to keep their IT infrastructure inside the European Union.
Also:
7 things every Linux beginner should know before downloading their first distro
The
Digital Sovereignty
movement is a big deal in Europe for a reason. Today, over 90% of European data resides on servers operated by non-EU and primarily American companies. This dependency exposes EU entities to data privacy, economic leverage, and potential risks of foreign surveillance.
As a result, according to tech researcher IDC,
84% of European organizations using cloud technologies are either currently using or planning to use sovereign cloud solutions
. Rahiel Nasir, IDC's research director for European Cloud Strategies, described 2025 as a "watershed year," with growing geopolitical and economic uncertainties putting digital sovereignty at the forefront for organizations.
Also:
Linux's remarkable journey from one dev's hobby to 40 million lines of code - and counting
That's why SUSE, a global leader in enterprise open-source solutions, has announced the launch of its Sovereign Premium Support package. This comprehensive support service is designed to meet the growing demand for digital sovereignty.
Specifically, Dirk-Peter (DP) van Leeuwen, SUSE's CEO, explained: "For some, it's a brand new story. But for us,
digital sovereignty
is old news. We've been enabling it for years for our customers. Along the way, we've learned you have to get three main things right: Data, technology, and operations. The last area -- business operations -- is often least looked at, but it's often the hardest to deliver. Ultimately, it is about the people -- where are they? And how do we ensure we have the scale to deliver business continuity? That's what we're addressing with the launch of SUSE Sovereign Premium Support."
Also:
I put Linux on this 8-inch mini laptop, and unlocked a new way of computing
In practice, SUSE's Sovereign Premium Support is tailored for enterprises and public sector organizations that require strict data residency, privacy, and operational control within the EU. The service ensures that:
All support personnel and data are based in the EU, with named premium support engineers and service delivery managers assigned to each customer.
Customer support data is stored exclusively on EU-located networks and servers, addressing both regulatory and geopolitical concerns.
Access to sensitive data is strictly limited to EU-based staff, with a commitment to encrypting all data required for troubleshooting.
This approach directly responds to the evolving landscape of European regulations and the heightened focus on digital independence. While it's an approach meant specifically for areas such as defense, government, and law enforcement, where compliance and resilience are paramount, it's being offered to all European organizations.
As Udo Wuertz, CDO and fellow at the data center company
Fsas Technologies Europe
, said, SUSE's "Open by Design, Sovereign by Choice" philosophy, combined with enhanced EU-based support, provides tailored solutions for customers with stringent sovereignty requirements.
Also:
Can't upgrade your Windows 10 PC? Here are your options before it all ends in 3 months
If this focus sounds paranoid, well, the world has changed. There's more geopolitical uncertainty today than since the Cold War threatened to get hot. So, for Europeans, SUSE's new program may be just what they need to feel secure again. SUSE stands ready to help with its Linux, open-source, and cloud offerings.
Contact SUSE
to learn more about their latest service.

data.title: Springer Nature book on machine learning is full of made-up citations
data.author: ArmageddonIt
data.article_summary: 《Mastering Machine Learning》一书由Springer Nature出版，但被发现包含大量虚假或错误的引用。在检查的18条引用中，三分之二要么不存在，要么有重大错误。一些被引用的研究者确认他们的工作要么未正式发表，要么被错误引用。该书作者Govindakumar Madhavan未回应是否使用了大型语言模型（LLM）生成内容，但虚假引用是LLM生成文本的常见问题。Springer Nature表示正在调查此事，并强调其政策要求作者在使用AI时需声明并有人工监督。LLM生成内容引发的学术诚信问题正日益受到关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容在出版物中的使用及其引发的问题

不同观点：
• [misja111] 认为作者没有明确回答是否使用了大型语言模型（LLM）生成书籍内容，并对作者关于辨别AI生成内容的难度回应表示怀疑，暗示该回应本身可能也是AI生成的。
• [haffi112] 指出，像Springer这样的知名品牌应进行尽职调查，以确保出版物的质量，并认为这是一个通过可验证性来增加品牌价值的机会，但Springer显然没有做到这一点。
• [ludicrousdispla] 强调，LLM的整个输出都是编造的，即使是看起来合法的引用也可能是不真实的。
• [alok-g] 提出，开发和使用引用检查工具可以部分解决引用问题，但文本中的声明是否经过验证或正确仍是一个未解决的问题。
• [Isamu] 希望AI能用于自动化引用查找和验证，但目前AI却在制造问题，显示出激励机制的不一致。
• [veltas] 认为教材质量低下的问题早已存在，学生和讲师往往不加辨别地使用这些书籍。
• [techas] 提到在一些会议摘要中也发现了类似的问题，即引用看起来真实但并不存在。
• [b00ty4breakfast] 对AI生成内容的未来表示担忧，并暗示缺乏信心。
• [Vinayak_A_B] 提出开发引用验证工具的可能性，并设想其在会议和期刊中的应用。
• [amelius] 质疑整本书是否由机器生成，或者是否是人类文本加上机器生成的引用。
• [MarlonPro] 对喜欢书籍作为学习资源的人表示同情，暗示AI生成内容对传统书籍构成威胁。
• [PeterStuer] 幽默地提出是否可以通过占据不存在的引用成为“最常被引用的作者”。
• [zero_k] 批评Springer在处理同行评审研究论文时的表现，暗示对该出版社的失望。
• [dandanua] 描绘了一个出版业的未来，即AI在书籍和文章的写作、评审和编辑中占据主导地位，使出版社继续从机构订阅中获利。
• [MengerSponge] 用幽默的方式表达了对AI生成内容和剽窃问题的关注。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成内容的可信度和质量问题，尤其是引用和验证的真实性。
• 讨论中多次提到Springer等出版商的品牌信誉和质量控制问题。
• 有人提出技术解决方案，如引用检查工具，但也有对技术应用现实性的质疑和幽默评论。
• 对AI生成内容在学术和出版领域的未来影响存在担忧和讽刺。

44507061.article_content:
Would you pay $169 for an introductory ebook on machine learning with citations that appear to be made up?
If not, you might want to pass on purchasing
Mastering Machine Learning: From Basics to Advanced
, published by Springer Nature in April.
Based on a tip from a reader, we checked 18 of the 46 citations in the book. Two-thirds of them either did not exist or had substantial errors. And three researchers cited in the book confirmed the works they supposedly authored were fake or the citation contained substantial errors.
“We wrote this paper and it was not formally published,” said Yehuda Dar, a computer scientist at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, whose work was cited in the book. “It is an arXiv preprint.” The citation incorrectly states the paper appeared in
IEEE Signal Processing Magazine
.
Aaron Courville, a professor of computer science at Université de Montréal and coauthor on the book
Deep Learning
, was correctly cited for the text itself, but for a section that “doesn’t seem to exist,” he said. “Certainly not at pages 194-201.” And Dimitris Kalles of Hellenic Open University in Greece also confirmed he did not write a cited work listing him as the author.
The researcher who emailed us, and asked to remain anonymous, had received an alert from Google Scholar about the book, which cited him. While his name appeared on multiple citations, the cited works do not exist.
Nonexistent and error-prone citations are a
hallmark of text generated by large language models like ChatGPT
. These models don’t search literature databases for published papers like a human author would. Instead, they generate content based on training data and prompts. So LLM-generated citations might look legitimate, but the content of the citations might be fabricated.
The book’s author, Govindakumar Madhavan, asked for an additional “week or two” to fully respond to our request for comment. He did not answer our questions asking if he used an LLM to generate text for the book. However, he told us, “reliably determining whether content (or an issue) is AI generated remains a challenge, as even human-written text can appear ‘AI-like.’ This challenge is only expected to grow, as LLMs … continue to advance in fluency and sophistication.”
According to his bio in the book, Madhavan is the founder and CEO of SeaportAi and author of about 40 video courses and 10 books. The 257-page book includes a section on ChatGPT that states: “the technology raises important ethical questions about the use and misuse of AI-generated text.”
Springer Nature provides
policies and guidance
about the use of AI to its authors, Felicitas Behrendt, senior communications manager for books at the publisher, told us by email. “Whilst we recognise that authors may use LLMs, we emphasise that any submission must be undertaken with full human oversight, and any AI use beyond basic copy editing must be declared.”
Mastering Machine Learning
contains no such declaration. When asked about the potential use of AI in the work, Behrendt told us: “We are aware of the text and are currently looking into it.” She did not comment on efforts taken during Springer Nature’s editorial process to ensure its AI policies are followed.
LLM-generated citations were at the center of controversies around Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s
“Make America Healthy Again” report
and a CDC presentation on the
vaccine preservative thimerosal
. At Retraction Watch, our cofounders
were once cited in a made-up reference
in an Australian government report on research integrity.  We’ve seen fake citations fell
research
articles
, and
our list of papers
with evidence of undisclosed ChatGPT use has grown long and almost certainly represents
only a fraction
of those that actually do.
The same day Behrendt replied to our query, Springer Nature published a post on its blog titled, “
Research integrity in books: Prevention by balancing human oversight and AI tools
.”
“All book manuscripts are initially assessed by an in-house editor who decides whether to forward the submission to further review,” Deidre Hudson Reuss, senior content marketing manager at the company, wrote. “The reviewers – subject matter experts – evaluate the manuscript’s quality and originality, to ensure its validity and that it meets the highest integrity and ethics standards.”

data.article_summary: PHP团队宣布推出PHP 8.5.0的第一个测试版本Alpha 1，标志着8.5版本周期的开始。此版本仅供测试，不建议用于生产环境。用户可从下载页面获取源码，并可在GitHub上报告发现的问题。有关新功能和变更的详细信息，可查阅NEWS文件，升级注意事项则在UPGRADING文件中。下一个版本Alpha 2计划于2025年7月17日发布。签名可在manifest或发布候选页面找到。感谢社区帮助改进PHP。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PHP 8.5的新特性和Unicode支持问题

不同观点：
• [moebrowne] 对PHP 8.5引入的新管道操作符（pipe operator）表示关注，并提供了一个相关博客链接，介绍了这一新特性。他认为这一更新值得注意，显示出对新功能持积极态度。

• [phplovesong] 则对PHP的Unicode支持不足表示不满，特别是对缺乏内建的Unicode处理功能，如统一的字符处理函数。他批评开发团队没有解决这一长期存在的问题，并继续依赖于mb_*系列函数来处理多字节字符串。

补充讨论：
• [phplovesong] 的评论暗示了对PHP开发团队优先级的质疑，认为在引入新特性的同时，核心功能（如Unicode支持）仍然被忽视。
• [phplovesong] 使用了较为情绪化的语言（"what in the hell are the devs doing?"），显示出对这一问题强烈的失望情绪。
• 争议的焦点在于PHP在引入新特性和解决现有功能不足之间的优先级和资源分配问题。一部分开发者可能更关注新功能的引入以保持语言的现代性，而另一部分开发者则希望优先解决长期存在的功能性问题。

44507284.article_content:
03 Jul 2025
The PHP team is pleased to announce the first testing release of PHP 8.5.0, Alpha 1. This starts the PHP 8.5 release cycle, the rough outline of which is specified in the
PHP Wiki
.
For source downloads of PHP 8.5.0 Alpha 1 please visit the
download page
.
Please carefully test this version and report any issues found
on GitHub
.
Please DO NOT use this version in production, it is an early test version.
For more information on the new features and other changes, you can read the
NEWS
file, or the
UPGRADING
file for a complete list of upgrading notes. These files can also be found in the release archive.
The next release will be Alpha 2, planned for 17 Jul 2025.
The signatures for the release can be found in the
manifest
or on the
Release Candidates page
.
Thank you for helping us make PHP better.

data.title: ESIM Security
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Security Explorations公司旗下的研究实验室对eSIM技术进行了安全分析，特别是Kigen的eUICC卡。研究表明，eUICC卡在安装特定Java应用程序时存在安全漏洞，攻击者可通过物理访问和掌握密钥进行恶意操作，甚至可能通过SMS-PP协议进行远程攻击。尽管Kigen声称其eSIM卡具有高度安全性和互操作性，并通过GSMA多层认证，但此次破解显示eUICC在内存内容保护和Java应用程序隔离方面存在缺陷。研究还证实了2019年报告给Oracle的Java Card漏洞确实存在，并首次公开了对消费级GSMA eUICC的成功攻击。此次研究强调了eSIM安全问题，呼吁移动网络运营商和安全公司加强防护措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一篇关于GSM/eSIM技术的文章及相关安全问题的评论分析

不同观点：
• [mathfailure] 认为该文章写得非常好，即使作为一个外行，他也能够理解文章中的内容，并对文章的清晰度表示赞赏。
• [Fethbita] 则关注Oracle在解决eSIM安全问题上的不作为，认为这会对整个eSIM生态系统造成威胁，表现出对企业责任的强烈不满。
• [hhh] 评论文章的技术质量很高，并认为其价值远超3万美元，显示出对技术工作的认可。
• [rs_rs_rs_rs_rs] 简短地赞扬了文章的来源（lsd-pl团队），但没有深入讨论技术细节。

补充讨论：
• [exabrial] 对文章中提到的"对密钥的了解是目标卡妥协的主要要求"提出疑问，并通过PGP密钥的例子请求进一步解释，显示出对技术细节的关注和求知欲。
• [ACCount36] 表达了对未修复硬件的公开概念验证（PoC）的期待，并提到他长期以来一直在寻找一种方法来以明文形式转储eSIM，暗示对技术漏洞利用的兴趣。
• [daft_pink] 提出一个附带问题，询问中国是否会采用eSIM技术，显示出对eSIM技术推广范围的关注。
• [petesergeant] 则从一个更广泛的角度出发，认为在任何严重的战争初期，电信服务将会完全瘫痪，反映出对电信安全的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 对于Oracle在解决eSIM安全问题上的不作为，[Fethbita] 表达了强烈的不满，认为这会危及整个eSIM生态系统，而其他评论者未直接涉及此问题。
• 对密钥泄露的潜在威胁，[exabrial] 提出了具体的技术疑问，显示出对细节的关注，而其他评论者未对此进行深入讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕文章的易懂性、技术质量、企业责任、技术漏洞利用的兴趣以及对eSIM技术推广和安全的关注展开。不同评论者从各自的角度出发，提出了对文章内容、技术细节及相关安全问题的各种看法。

General info
In a result of its research investigation efforts, Security Explorations, a research lab of AG Security Research company, conducted security analysis of eSIM technology.
This section of our website presents initial information regarding the project.
Notes
We broke security of
Kigen
(*)
eUICC
card with
GSMA
consumer certificates installed into it.
The eUICC card makes it possible to install the so called eSIM profiles into target chip. eSIM profiles are software representations of mobile subscriptions. For many years such mobile subscriptions had a form of a physical
SIM card
of various factors (SIM, microSIM, nonoSIM). With eSIM, the subscription can come in a pure digital form (as a software bundle), it can also carry Java Card applications.
According to Kigen:
1) eSIMs are "as secure and interoperable as SIM cards [...] thanks to the multi-layered GSMA eSIM certification scheme that protects device makers, device owners and mobile network operators (MNOs)" (
source
)
2) "Kigen OS offers the highest level of logical security when employed on any SIM form factor, including a secure enclave" and "Kigen SIM OS features help differentiate, scale and grow revenues with zero compromise security" (
source
)
The hack proves that our
research on Java Card from 2019
did matter. Oracle indicated the
vulnerabilities we reported
to the company in 2019 were rather irrelevant (the company referred to them as "security concerns") / did not affect their production Java Card VM. These are now proved to be real bugs.
This is likely the first successful public hack against:
consumer GSMA eUICC
Kigen eSIM (Kigen
press releases
and
web pages
implicate over 2 billion SIMs enabled by Kigen secure SIM OS)
EAL(**) certified GSMA security chip (
SLC37 chip
based on 32-bit ARM SecurCore SC300 processor from
Infineon
)
The attack against Kigen eUICC relies both on physical access to sample card along knowledge of the keys used for malicious Java app installation. The remote over-the-air (OTA) vector can't be excluded - our Proof of Concept code mimics a malicious applet installation over OTA
SMS-PP protocol
(Short Message Service Point to Point) on a target Kigen eUICC. In that context, knowledge of the keys is a primary requirement for target card compromise.
The hack proves no security / isolation for the eSIM profile and Java apps (no security for eUICC memory content).
It's worth to note that while this work builds on our past Java Card research from 2019 (along [
25
] [
years
] [
of
] [
Java
] [
hacking
] experience), it required development of some new exploitation techniques / know-how.
We hope the hack brings eSIM security along associated security risks to the focus of mobile network operators (MNOs), vendors, security researchers and security companies. This is important in the context of somewhat bold security claims / overconfidence of eUICC vendors (vide
leaf eUICC cert valid for 100 years
) and MNO assumptions pertaining to profile trust and its storage in a tamper-proof security element (MNO profile integrity / no compromise / no tampering assumed).
(*) as denoted by eUICC / EUM certificates and card EID
(**)
RSP specification
impose minimum EAL4 level ("4.14.1 eUICC Certification Requirements", page 55)
Crypto Proof
As a result of eUICC compromise, we were able to extract private
ECC
key for the certificate
