Dark Mode Toggle
Why I used to prefer permissive licenses and now favor copyleft
2025 Jul 07
See all posts
Why I used to prefer permissive licenses and now favor copyleft
Within
free
open source software
(and
free content
more
generally), there are two major categories of copyright licenses:
If content is published with a
permissive license
(eg.
CC0
,
MIT
), anyone can take
it and use it and redistribute it for any purpose with no restrictions,
perhaps with minimal rules requiring
attribution
.
If content is published with a
copyleft license
(eg.
CC-BY-SA
,
GPL
), anyone
can take it and use it and redistribute copies with no restrictions, but
if you create and distribute a
derivative work
by modifying it
or combining it with other work, the new work must also be released
under the same license. Additionally, GPL requires any derivative work
to openly publish its source code, in addition to
a
few other requirements
.
In summary:
permissive licenses freely share with everyone,
copyleft licenses freely share only with those who are also willing to
freely share
.
I have been a fan of, and developer of, free open source software and
free content ever since I've been old enough to understand what these
things are and build things that I thought other people might find
useful. Historically, I was a fan of the permissive approach (eg. my
blog is under the
WTFPL
). More
recently, I am warming up to the copyleft approach. This post explains
my reasons why.
One style of software freedom, promoted by the
WTFPL
. But not the only style.
Why I was
historically a fan of permissive licenses
First, I wanted to
maximize adoption and
distribution
of my work, and releasing it under permissive
licenses facilitates that, by making it clear that there is
nothing
anyone needs to worry about if they want to build off
of something I make. Enterprises are often unwilling to release their
projects freely, and given that I did not see myself having any ability
to nudge them to fully join the free software side, I wanted to avoid
being needlessly incompatible with the approach they already had and
would not give up.
Second,
I generally philosophically dislike
copyright
(and patents). I dislike the idea that two people
privately sharing bits of data between each other can be perceived as
committing a crime against a third party whom they are not touching or
even communicating with and are not taking anything away from (no, "not
paying" is NOT the same as "stealing"). Explicitly releasing to public
domain is
legally
complicated for various reasons
, and so a permissive license is the
cleanest and safest way to get as close as possible to not copyrighting
your works.
I do appreciate the copyleft idea of "using copyright against
itself"
- it's a beautiful legal hack. In some ways it's
similar what I always found philosophically beautiful about
libertarianism. As a political philosophy, it's often described as
banishing the use of violent force except for one application: to
protect people from other violent force. As a social philosophy, I
sometimes see it as a way of taming the harmful effects of the human
disgust reflex by making freedom itself a
sacred
thing that we find it disgusting to defile: even if you think two other
people having an unusual consensual sexual relationship is disgusting,
you can't go after them, because interfering in the private lives of
free human beings is itself disgusting. So in principle, there are
historical precedents to show that disliking copyright is compatible
with using copyright against itself.
However, while copyleft
of written work
fits into this
definition,
GPL-style copyright of code
oversteps
beyond a minimalistic notion of "using copyright against itself",
because it offensively uses copyright for a different purpose: mandating
publication of source code
. This is a public-spirited purpose,
and not a selfish purpose of collecting licensing fees, but it is
nevertheless an offensive use of copyright. This becomes even more true
for stricter licenses like the
AGPL
, which
require publication of source code of derivative works even if you never
publish them and only make them available via software-as-a-service.
Different types of software licenses, with different sets
of conditions under which someone making a derivative work is required
to share the source code. Some of them require publishing source code
under a wide variety of situations.
Why I am warmer to copyleft
today
My switch from favoring permissive to favoring copyleft is motivated
by two world events and one philosophical shift.
First,
open source has become mainstream, and nudging
enterprises toward it is much more practical
. Plenty of
companies in all kinds of industries are embracing open source.
Companies like
Google
,
Microsoft
and
Huawei
are embracing
open source, and even building major software packages open. New
industries, including AI and of course crypto, are heavier on open
source than previous industries ever were.
Second,

  - 有人认为在超线性规模收益的情况下，适度推动项目开放比严格的产权保护更优，支持某种程度上的主动开放政策。
  - 有人质疑如果允许更大规模的经济体形成，是否会加速研究进展，认为最佳的公司与用户关系应该是共生的，而非对抗性的。

补充讨论：
• **对"宽松许可"的命名争议**：
  - 有人认为“宽松许可”这个名称有误导性，因为它从软件中间商的角度出发，而非用户角度。
  - 指出copyleft许可实际上赋予用户更多权限，例如查看和修改源代码，而宽松许可可能让第三方剥夺这些权限。

• **对特定人物和事件的调侃**：
  - 有评论调侃以太坊创始人Vitalik参与讨论，并质疑是否因某些代码被专有化而希望其开源。
  - 有人提到“加密兄弟”在重新发现RMS（Richard Stallman）多年前的自由软件理念。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于版权保护许可与宽松许可的选择，前者注重代码的持续开放和用户的自由，后者强调代码的自由使用和最小化使用者的义务。
• 技术扩散与知识产权保护之间的平衡也是讨论中的一个争议点，涉及如何在开放与专有之间找到最佳路径。

data.title: Federal court in Colorado fines lawyers for errors caused by use of "AI"
data.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：律师使用AI生成法律文件中的虚假引用问题及其责任

不同观点：
• [burnt-resistor的观点]  
认为应采取对懒散、马虎的职业不当行为零容忍的态度。建议像LexisNexis和Westlaw这样的法律研究工具应开发更多工具来自动检查文件引用的有效性，以避免虚假引用问题。

• [rmunn的观点]  
解释了美国法律程序中的联邦民事诉讼规则（Federal Rules of Civil Procedure），尤其是第11条规则，规定提交法院的文件需有法律依据或合理论证。强调了LLM（如AI）生成法律文件时可能出现"幻觉"（即编造内容），特别是引用案例时的错误风险。指出无论文件是由AI、法律秘书还是律师助理起草，律师都应对文件中的错误负责。在本案中，律师因未仔细检查AI生成的文件而提交了包含虚假引用的文件，被法院罚款。

补充讨论：
• 责任归属  
rmunn详细说明了尽管使用了AI生成文件，律师仍然有责任检查文件的准确性。引用案例的真实性和对论点支持的有效性都需要律师亲自确认。

• AI工具的局限性  
burnt-resistor和rmunn都提到了AI工具在处理法律文件时的局限性，尤其是引用方面的"幻觉"问题。burnt-resistor建议法律研究平台应开发更多验证工具，而rmunn则强调了律师在使用AI工具时需格外谨慎。

• 法院的处理  
rmunn描述了法院对使用AI工具生成错误文件的处理方式，明确指出律师对提交文件中的错误负有责任，并举例说明了本案中律师因未尽检查责任而被罚款的具体情况。

争议焦点：
• 责任划分  
虽然使用AI生成文件可能提高效率，但文件中错误的法律责任仍归属于律师。这一责任划分在实际操作中可能引发争议，尤其是在AI工具日益普及的情况下，如何平衡技术便利与法律责任成为讨论的关键。

data.title: Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business
data.author: jonkuipers
data.article_summary: Kyle Nolan分享了他如何在零资金的情况下，通过副业项目打造了一个年收入达到100万美元的业务。2021年，Kyle受财务独立运动启发，因找不到合适的财务规划工具，决定自行开发ProjectionLab。从2021年5月的150美元月 recurring revenue（MRR）开始，他利用业余时间开发项目，逐步增加收入并在2023年全职投入。随着收入增长，Kyle在2024年组建团队，并最终在2025年达到100万美元的年 recurring revenue（ARR）。尽管过程中经历了收入波动和自我怀疑，Kyle坚持不懈，并认识到不放弃是创业成功的关键。他与Jon Kuipers合作负责增长和营销，并从用户社区中招募团队成员，以提供优质的客户体验。

We reached $1M ARR with zero funding
Kyle Nolan

Jun 30, 2025
Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business in four years.
We really did it! We bootstrapped ProjectionLab to $1,000,000 in annual recurring revenue.
And I’m still processing that this is real. 🥹
Back in 2021, I was inspired by the financial independence movement and wanted a better way to plan my own life. I couldn’t find the right tool, so I started building.
I had no idea that side project would one day help over 100,000 households plan for their financial future too.
How we got here
If this is your first time hearing about ProjectionLab, here’s a quick recap:
Milestone

What Was Happening

May 2021

post to HN
)

Shoutout from Mr Money Mustache

Whoah, public speaking?!

Started to believe I could do this
$10K MRR
Jun 2023
The final boss of indie hacking
$16.6K MRR

Dropped to part-time at my day job
$23.3K MRR
Nov 2023
Quit my day job and went all-in!
$41.6K MRR
Jul 2024
Started growing the team
$45.8K MRR
Aug 2024
Shared story on ChooseFI
$83.3k MRR
Jun 2025
👋 Here we are!
When you look beyond the recurring revenue chart, this journey had ups, downs, and moments I wanted to quit.
The emotions behind the numbers
Want to know what building in public from zero to a million dollars a year really felt like? NOT like serenely progressing up-and-to-the-right…
More like riding a dopamine rollercoaster while getting attacked by a bear.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The flat months in the early years? The dips in earnings? The times I woke up to a dozen canceled subscriptions?
Each one had me questioning everything, wondering if I should just focus on the corporate ladder, or maybe try to get into big tech instead.
The financial independence movement is what set me on this path. So on top of worrying about normal business risks, I was primed to think in terms of my time and opportunity cost, and how failure would hurt my own timeline to FI.
But gradually, I learned that emotional peaks and valleys are always a part of entrepreneurship. And that “not giving up” is actually a superpower.
Not giving up
There are loads of people out there smarter than me.
But luckily, success indexes less on IQ and more on consistency. The willingness to doggedly show up every single day can take you to some really suprising and amazing places.
And you know what makes it easier and more rewarding to be that persistent?
Working alongside people you like.
From solo dev to real team
For the first two years, I burned the candle at both ends working solo. 4-6 hours every night after work, entire weekends, holidays, you name it.
404 Day Off Not Found.
That was the only way I could build something this complex in a crowded market as a risk-averse engineer with a day job. And I was fortunate enough to attempt this at a stage in life when I had lots of energy and few family responsibilities.
Plus my trusty sidekick, BB the bird:
But long-term, I knew there would be a choice to face:
Keep doing everything myself and watch growth plateau, or…
Find someone with a complementary skillset and start building a team.
I was just an ordinary engineer with zero marketing experience. So I figured I should try to team up with someone good at growth & marketing.
Finding a growth & marketing partner
During the first few years, I was approached by dozens of potential “partners.” Several wanted an outsize equity stake to essentially just make suggestions. Others had the wrong skillset or didn’t feel like a complete fit.
But
Jon Kuipers
jumped right into the trenches and worked to prove himself before asking for anything. He spent a year contributing real value, and when the time came to bring on a growth partner full-time, I didn’t look anywhere else.
Now I stay focused on building, while he handles growth, marketing, partnerships, and some ops stuff.
Building a team
We’ve also added a few contractors to the team.
And these guys are legends. 💪
They come straight from the ProjectionLab user community, and they are doing a great job fielding the arcane finance questions our customers love to ask. Plus hosting 1-on-1 sessions, creating
tutorial videos
, and more.
Could we have offshored customer success for pennies on the dollar instead? You bet. But having a happy and engaged user community of product evangelists means a lot to us, and I want them all to have the best experience possible.
For multiple years, I was up at all hours answering support questions myself. It interrupted my dev work (and my sleep) constantly. I love the PL community – it’s a big part of what motivated me to keep going back then.
And it blows my mind that the empty discord

data.title: A lightweight Cloudflare Dynamic DNS shell script
data.author: fernvenue
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个轻量级的Cloudflare动态DNS shell脚本（cloudflare-ddns），支持IPv4和IPv6双栈、多记录更新、智能监控（仅在IP变化时更新）、自动缓存、多种认证方式（API Token和Legacy API Key）、代理协议支持、Systemd支持、Telegram通知、CSV日志记录等功能。用户可以通过环境变量或命令行参数配置脚本，并使用systemd服务和定时器实现自动运行。CSV日志默认启用，记录更新历史，存储位置可以配置。脚本还提供了详细的命令行选项和使用说明。

: Only updates DNS records when IP address changes;
Auto Caching
: Automatically caches DNS records and zone information for improved performance;
Multiple Authentication Support
: Support for both Cloudflare API Token and Legacy API Key authentication;
Proxy Protocol Support
: Support for configuring Socks proxy for API requests;
Systemd Support
: Provides service/timer examples and dynamic user support;
Telegram Push
: Highly readable Telegram notification push;
CSV Logging
: Automatic logging of DNS updates to CSV file for history tracking and analysis;
Flexible Configuration
: Support for command line parameter passing and environment variable configuration;
Usage
Get the script:
curl -o /usr/local/bin/cloudflare-ddns.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fernvenue/cloudflare-ddns/refs/heads/master/cloudflare-ddns.sh
vim /usr/local/bin/cloudflare-ddns.sh
Give it executable permission and run.
Make sure the corresponding domain already has records before running
, otherwise the script cannot find the records to update.
For detailed help information, you can use:
./cloudflare-ddns.sh --help

: API Token of your Cloudflare account (recommended);

true

不同观点：
• jerpint认为，许多公司已经意识到无法阻止提示（prompt）的泄露，有些公司甚至选择公开发布提示。这种做法可以减少模糊性，因为即便泄露的提示可能存在虚构成分，但公开发布提示有助于澄清问题。
   
• kubb则对jerpint的观点表示怀疑，认为所展示的提示不应如此简短。kubb指出，一个完整的提示应该包含工具的使用方法、编码指南等具体内容，而不仅仅是简短的一段话。

补充讨论：
• jerpint的立场基于提示泄露无法避免的现实，并认为公开提示可以减少误解和不确定性，即使泄露内容可能存在不准确之处。
   
• kubb则关注提示的完整性和实用性，强调一个有效的提示应该包括更详细的操作指南和技术细节，否则可能无法有效指导使用者。

争议的焦点在于提示是否应该公开发布，以及一个有效的提示应该包含哪些具体内容。jerpint倾向于接受提示泄露并认为公开能带来好处，而kubb则关注提示的质量和完整性。

data.article_summary: 在2025年7月4日华盛顿州塔克维拉的ICE办公楼抗议活动中，Straight Arrow News通过专门软件"Marlin"检测到手机监控的证据。分析显示，移动网络异常与IMSI捕捉器（也称"Stingray"）的使用一致，这种设备可以收集手机的识别信息。ICE未回应是否获得授权使用该设备。IMSI捕捉器常用于定位或追踪手机，但其使用需经过法院授权。美国公民自由联盟指出，若该技术被用于监控抗议者，政府需承担重大责任。此类设备不仅被执法机构使用，也被犯罪分子利用，可能导致敏感信息泄露。

Tech
Exclusive: Evidence of cell phone surveillance detected at anti-ICE protest
Jul 09, 2025 at 01:02 PM CDT
Mikael Thalen
(Tech Reporter),
Simone Del Rosario
(Vice President of Talent Strategy and Development)
Copy URL
Email
Facebook
Twitter / X
Reddit
Listen
.
This recording was made using enhanced software.
Summary
Evidence of surveillance
An independent analysis of cellular traffic by Straight Arrow News uncovered evidence of cell phone surveillance.
ICE protest
The mobile network anomalies were detected with specialized software during a protest at an ICE field office on July 4.
'Marlin' detection
The detection was made possible due to a tool called “Marlin,” developed by mobile security experts at the University of Florida and ETH Zurich.
Read full story
Full story
Mobile network anomalies consistent with cell phone surveillance were detected at a July 4 protest at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement field office in Washington state. Those anomalies, according to an independent analysis by Straight Arrow News, suggest that a device known as an IMSI catcher may have been used to collect identifying information on cell phones at the protest site.
ICE did not respond to requests for comment from SAN. It is not clear whether ICE or any other law enforcement agency obtained a warrant to use an IMSI catcher — commonly referred to as a “Stingray” — to conduct surveillance.
Download the SAN app today to stay up-to-date with Unbiased. Straight Facts™.
Point phone camera here
The ICE field office in Tukwila, Washington, a Seattle suburb, has been the site of repeated protests over President Donald Trump’s immigration policies. When an estimated 200 protesters gathered outside the facility on June 14, local police officers used
pepper spray
to break up the demonstration. Far fewer protesters came to the facility on July 4.
Federal law enforcement agencies may use IMSI catchers without a warrant only in “exigent” or “exceptional circumstances,” according to a 2023 report by the Department of Homeland Security’s
inspector general
. Those circumstances include immediate threats to national security and situations where a person is in danger of death or serious injury.
The inspector general found that ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations unit and the Secret Service had used the devices for surveillance without proper court authorization. The report redacted the number of instances the inspector general cited or the reasons for not obtaining a warrant.
Nathan Freed Wessler, deputy director with the
ACLU’s Speech, Privacy and Technology Project
, said the use of a Stingray device “to identify or track people exercising their First Amendment right to protest would raise grave concerns.”
“There is good reason why courts have held that this invasive technology can only be used in limited circumstances after securing a valid warrant,” Wessler told SAN. “If evidence were to show these devices being targeted at protesters, the government would have a lot to answer for.”
Device used by law enforcement, criminals
An IMSI catcher is a type of cell-site simulator designed to mimic a cell tower. When activated, it can force a connection with mobile phones as far as a third of a mile away, tricking them into revealing their IMSI, or International Mobile Subscriber Identity.
An IMSI is a unique 15-digit number tied to a cell phone’s SIM card that cellular networks use to identify users.
Law enforcement
and
intelligence agencies
use IMSI catchers to pinpoint the location of a specific phone or to record the presence of all phones in a designated area.
Criminals have also been known to leverage the technology, which can be built with publicly available components and software. They can deliver malware to targeted devices, potentially compromising sensitive information and enabling further attacks.
More advanced IMSI catchers can force cell phones to downgrade to less secure protocols, such as 2G, enabling the collection of unencrypted text messages and phone calls.
Anomalies suggest surveillance
SAN analyzed LTE cellular traffic at an anti-ICE protest in Tukwila, using a tool called Marlin that was
developed
by teams at the University of Florida and Switzerland’s ETH Zurich. About 20 people attended the protest, organized by the local chapter of the progressive grassroots organization
Indivisible
.
The analysis uncovered unusual bursts of data, known as “IMSI-exposing messages,” across several LTE frequency bands. Normally, cell phones are provided Temporary International Mobile Subscriber Identities, or TIMSIs, by networks for privacy purposes. Legitimate cell towers rarely request a cell phone’s permanent IMSI, which can be used to identify and track individuals.
At 8:58 a.m., just before the protest began, SAN began monitoring eight LTE bands present in the area and found no anomalous behavior. At 9:06 a.m., however, a burst of 57 IMSI-exposing commands was detected.

data.title: US Court nullifies FTC requirement for click-to-cancel
data.author: gausswho
data.article_summary: 美国联邦上诉法院推翻了联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的一项“点击取消”规则，该规则要求公司使取消服务与注册一样简便。法院认为，FTC在制定规则过程中未遵循完整的程序，特别是未进行初步监管分析，而这一步骤在预计年度经济影响超过1亿美元时是强制要求的。尽管FTC辩称其无需进行初步分析，且在最终规则中分析了替代方案和合规成本，但法院认为其分析过于简略，未给予行业团体足够时间提出异议。此判决由第八巡回法院的三名法官做出，其中包括两名特朗普任命的法官。这一决定也得到了多个行业团体的支持，他们起诉FTC未遵循适当程序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FTC在处理负面选择营销规则时是否遵循了必要的程序，以及该裁决对消费者和企业的影响。

不同观点：
• ApolloFortyNine：认为法官依据法律而非情感做出裁决，FTC未遵循必要的程序，特别是在影响超过1亿美元的规则时，应该进行初步的监管分析。法官的裁决是合理的，以防止FTC和其它政府机构低估经济影响。
• John23832：认为该裁决只会保护企业利益，允许企业设置障碍以维持对消费者的剥削，批评FTC没有遵循规则制定程序，实际上是在为企业的不正当行为开脱。
• pjmlp：对比欧洲的消费者保护机制，认为FTC经常偏袒错误的一方，欧洲的消费者投诉通常能得到解决。
• beezlewax：以Brilliant平台为例，指出企业使用复杂取消流程和黑暗模式，消费者需要保护。
• everdrive：认为所有订阅服务都应被怀疑，取消服务的困难是一种隐藏成本。

补充讨论：
• fwlr：指出FTC曾被警告未遵循必要程序，最终裁决未能通过法律审查。
• nashashmi：建议FTC避免昂贵的规则制定，改为制定简单禁止复杂取消流程的规则，鼓励企业选择简单的取消选项。
• db48x：提供实际裁决文件链接供参考。
• bluetidepro：赞赏iOS商店简单的取消过程，认为通过iOS购买订阅值得，因为取消方便。
• xedrac：认为点击取消链接只是企业为了确认活跃账户并从中获利。
• charles_f：对23小时专业服务与1亿美元影响门槛的关系感到困惑。
• highwayman47：批评企业可以随意解除合同而消费者不能。
• throwaway_323：以apollo.io为例，指出企业使用黑暗模式和拒绝退款的行为，认为裁决不利于消费者。
• Narretz：建议国会制定相关法律，质疑国会是否仍在此类事务上立法。
• liendolucas：认为一次性卡片是目前避免被企业陷阱收费的最有效机制，希望未来情况能改善。

争议焦点：
• FTC是否遵循了必要的规则制定程序，以及该裁决是否主要有利于企业而非消费者。

A federal appeals court today struck down a "click-to-cancel" rule that would have required companies to make cancelling services as easy as signing up. The Federal Trade Commission rule was scheduled to take effect on July 14 but was vacated by the US Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit.
A three-judge panel ruled unanimously that the Biden-era FTC, then led by Chair Lina Khan, failed to follow the full rulemaking process required under US law. "While we certainly do not endorse the use of unfair and deceptive practices in negative option marketing, the procedural deficiencies of the Commission's rulemaking process are fatal here," the
ruling
said.
Indicating their sympathy with the FTC's motivations, judges wrote that many Americans "have found themselves unwittingly enrolled in recurring subscription plans, continuing to pay for unwanted products or services because they neglected to cancel their subscriptions." Last year, the FTC updated its 1973 Negative Option Rule by "adding provisions that bar sellers from misrepresenting material facts and require disclosure of material terms, express consumer consent, and a simple cancellation mechanism," the ruling said.
The FTC is required to conduct a preliminary regulatory analysis when a rule has an estimated annual economic effect of $100 million or more. The FTC estimated in a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) that the rule would not have a $100 million effect.
But an administrative law judge later found that the rule's impact surpassed the threshold, observing that compliance costs would exceed $100 million "unless each business used fewer than twenty-three hours of professional services at the lowest end of the spectrum of estimated hourly rates," the 8th Circuit ruling said. Despite the administrative law judge's finding, the FTC did not conduct a preliminary regulatory analysis and instead "proceeded to issue only the final regulatory analysis alongside the final Rule," the judges' panel said.
FTC arguments rejected
Summarizing the FTC's arguments, judges said the agency contended that US law "did not require the Commission to conduct the preliminary regulatory analysis later in the rulemaking process," and that "any alleged error was harmless because the NPRM addressed alternatives to the proposed amendments to the 1973 [Negative Option] Rule and analyzed record-keeping and compliance costs."
Judges disagreed with the FTC, writing that "the statutory language, 'shall issue,' mandates a separate preliminary analysis for public review and comment 'in any case' where the Commission issues a notice of proposed rulemaking and the $100 million threshold is surpassed."
Numerous industry groups and businesses,
including cable companies
, sued the FTC in four federal circuit courts. The cases were consolidated at the 8th Circuit, where it was decided by Circuit Judges James Loken, Ralph Erickson, and Jonathan Kobes. Loken was appointed by George H.W. Bush, while Erickson and Kobes are Trump appointees.
The judges said the lack of a preliminary analysis meant that industry groups and businesses weren't given enough time to contest the FTC's findings:
By the time the final regulatory analysis was issued, Petitioners still did not have the opportunity to assess the Commission's cost-benefit analysis of alternatives, an element of the preliminary regulatory analysis not required in the final analysis. And the Commission's discussion of alternatives in the final regulatory analysis was perfunctory. It briefly mentioned two alternatives to the final Rule, either terminating the rulemaking altogether and continuing to rely on the existing regulatory framework or limiting the Rule's scope to negative option plans marketed in-person or through the mail. While the Commission's decision to bypass the preliminary regulatory analysis requirement was certainly not made in bad faith or an "outright dodge of APA [Administrative Procedure Act] procedures," Petitioners have raised 'enough uncertainty whether [their] comments would have had some effect if they had been considered,' especially in the context of a closely divided Commission vote that elicited a lengthy dissenting statement.
The 8th Circuit ruling said the FTC's tactics, if not stopped, "could open the door to future manipulation of the rulemaking process. Furnishing an initially unrealistically low estimate of the economic impacts of a proposed rule would avail the Commission of a procedural shortcut that limits the need for additional public engagement and more substantive analysis of the potential effects of the rule on the front end."
Republicans opposed rule
The FTC
issued the proposal
in March 2023 and voted 3-2 to approve the rule
in October 2024
, with Republican Commissioners Melissa Holyoak and Andrew Ferguson voting against it. Ferguson is now chairman of the FTC,
44504699.article_summary: 美国联邦上诉法院推翻了联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的一项“点击取消”规则，该规则要求公司使取消服务与注册一样简便。法院认为，FTC在制定规则过程中未遵循完整的程序，特别是未进行初步监管分析，而这一步骤在预计年度经济影响超过1亿美元时是强制要求的。尽管FTC辩称其无需进行初步分析，且在最终规则中分析了替代方案和合规成本，但法院认为其分析过于简略，未给予行业团体足够时间提出异议。此判决由第八巡回法院的三名法官做出，其中包括两名特朗普任命的法官。这一决定也得到了多个行业团体的支持，他们起诉FTC未遵循适当程序。
44504699.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FTC在处理负面选择营销规则时是否遵循了必要的程序，以及该裁决对消费者和企业的影响。

不同观点：
• ApolloFortyNine：认为法官依据法律而非情感做出裁决，FTC未遵循必要的程序，特别是在影响超过1亿美元的规则时，应该进行初步的监管分析。法官的裁决是合理的，以防止FTC和其它政府机构低估经济影响。
• John23832：认为该裁决只会保护企业利益，允许企业设置障碍以维持对消费者的剥削，批评FTC没有遵循规则制定程序，实际上是在为企业的不正当行为开脱。
• pjmlp：对比欧洲的消费者保护机制，认为FTC经常偏袒错误的一方，欧洲的消费者投诉通常能得到解决。
• beezlewax：以Brilliant平台为例，指出企业使用复杂取消流程和黑暗模式，消费者需要保护。
• everdrive：认为所有订阅服务都应被怀疑，取消服务的困难是一种隐藏成本。

补充讨论：
• fwlr：指出FTC曾被警告未遵循必要程序，最终裁决未能通过法律审查。
• nashashmi：建议FTC避免昂贵的规则制定，改为制定简单禁止复杂取消流程的规则，鼓励企业选择简单的取消选项。
• db48x：提供实际裁决文件链接供参考。
• bluetidepro：赞赏iOS商店简单的取消过程，认为通过iOS购买订阅值得，因为取消方便。
• xedrac：认为点击取消链接只是企业为了确认活跃账户并从中获利。
• charles_f：对23小时专业服务与1亿美元影响门槛的关系感到困惑。
• highwayman47：批评企业可以随意解除合同而消费者不能。
• throwaway_323：以apollo.io为例，指出企业使用黑暗模式和拒绝退款的行为，认为裁决不利于消费者。

• liendolucas：认为一次性卡片是目前避免被企业陷阱收费的最有效机制，希望未来情况能改善。

• FTC是否遵循了必要的规则制定程序，以及该裁决是否主要有利于企业而非消费者。

data.title: Zorin OS
data.author: oldfuture
data.article_summary: Zorin OS 是一个专为替代 Windows 和 macOS 设计的操作系统，旨在让电脑运行更快、更强大、更安全、更注重隐私。它具有直观的用户界面，用户可以自定义桌面布局，使其类似于 Windows、macOS 或 Linux。Zorin OS 能在长达15年的老电脑上流畅运行，延长设备使用寿命并减少电子废物。基于 Ubuntu 和 Linux，它具备高安全性，能抵抗病毒和恶意软件，且不收集个人数据。系统自带必要应用程序，并支持运行许多 Windows 应用。它还提供游戏优化，兼容 Steam 等平台的游戏。通过 Zorin Connect，用户可以整合 Android 设备与电脑的体验。Zorin OS 可以与 Windows 或 macOS 双系统启动，且支持多语言和辅助技术。用户可以免费下载并试用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zorin OS的优缺点及是否适合不同类型的用户

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如olejorgenb）对Zorin OS的营销方式不满，认为技术细节不明显，需要用户主动寻找。
• afavour担心Zorin OS宣传的游戏和软件兼容性会导致用户遇到问题，认为ChromeOS更适合技术不熟练的用户。
• incanus77欣赏Zorin OS的整体设计和易用性，认为它是一个低麻烦、高完成度的系统，尽管可能在资源使用上不如其他定制化系统高效。
• replete在测试了多个Linux发行版后，认为Zorin OS最适合普通桌面用户，特别是习惯Windows的用户。
• LorenDB强调Zorin OS基于Ubuntu，兼容.deb包，并且没有Ubuntu的商业推广内容，非常适合新手。

补充讨论：
• puogue提供了Distro Sea网站和Zorin OS的评测视频资源，并提到Zorin的"pro"版本售价约50美元。
• roger_回忆了过去Linux笔记本的普及情况，并表达了对Linux在普通用户中推广的希望。
• trklausss关注Zorin OS网站上缺乏对开源软件和许可证合规性的提及，并质疑"pro"版本的GPL合规性。
• ThinkBeat使用过Zorin OS的"pro"版本，认为其升级价格不值得。
• jim201对Zorin OS出售包含免费开源软件的"pro"版本感到不满，认为这可能是不道德的。
• gxonatano批评Zorin OS过于注重模仿Windows或MacOS，忽视了Linux的创新潜力。

争议焦点：
• Zorin OS是否应该更透明地展示其技术细节和开源性质。
• Zorin OS对普通用户友好的特性是否牺牲了Linux的创新性和定制性。
• 出售包含开源软件的"pro"版本是否道德和合法。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 用户对Zorin OS在旧电脑上的表现给予积极评价。
• 一些用户认为Zorin OS在推广Linux给更广泛的用户群体方面具有潜力。

总结：
Zorin OS的讨论围绕其易用性、对普通用户的友好程度、开源软件的使用和合规性，以及其商业模式是否道德。不同用户根据自身经验和需求，对Zorin OS的优缺点有不同看法。

data.title: An analytic theory of creativity in convolutional diffusion models
data.author: foltik
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种解析、可解释且具有预测性的卷积扩散模型创造力理论。尽管得分匹配扩散模型能够生成远离训练数据的高度原创图像，但最佳得分匹配理论却表明这些模型只能生成记忆的训练样本。为弥合这一理论与实验的差距，作者识别了两种简单的归纳偏置——局部性和等变性，它们：(1) 通过防止最佳得分匹配来实现组合创造力；(2) 产生了完全解析且机械可解释的局部得分（LS）和等变局部得分（ELS）模型；(3) 在校准单个时间依赖的超参数后，能够高精度地预测训练后的卷积扩散模型（如ResNets和UNets）的输出。该模型揭示了一种局部一致的马赛克拼接创造力机制，通过在不同尺度和图像位置混合匹配不同的局部训练样本，扩散模型能够生成大量新颖图像。此外，该理论还部分预测了预训练的自注意力UNets的输出。

Computer Science > Machine Learning

(cs)

v1

Title:
An analytic theory of creativity in convolutional diffusion models
Authors:
Mason Kamb
,
Surya Ganguli
View a PDF of the paper titled An analytic theory of creativity in convolutional diffusion models, by Mason Kamb and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We obtain an analytic, interpretable and predictive theory of creativity in convolutional diffusion models. Indeed, score-matching diffusion models can generate highly original images that lie far from their training data. However, optimal score-matching theory suggests that these models should only be able to produce memorized training examples. To reconcile this theory-experiment gap, we identify two simple inductive biases, locality and equivariance, that: (1) induce a form of combinatorial creativity by preventing optimal score-matching; (2) result in fully analytic, completely mechanistically interpretable, local score (LS) and equivariant local score (ELS) machines that, (3) after calibrating a single time-dependent hyperparameter can quantitatively predict the outputs of trained convolution only diffusion models (like ResNets and UNets) with high accuracy (median $r^2$ of $0.95, 0.94, 0.94, 0.96$ for our top model on CIFAR10, FashionMNIST, MNIST, and CelebA). Our model reveals a locally consistent patch mosaic mechanism of creativity, in which diffusion models create exponentially many novel images by mixing and matching different local training set patches at different scales and image locations. Our theory also partially predicts the outputs of pre-trained self-attention enabled UNets (median $r^2 \sim 0.77$ on CIFAR10), revealing an intriguing role for attention in carving out semantic coherence from local patch mosaics.

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了C语言中`qsort`函数的历史问题及其数据传递的局限性，特别是在需要根据本地数据修改函数行为时。最初的`qsort`只接受一个函数指针，无法传递额外数据，导致开发者依赖`static`变量或全局变量，这在多线程和大型程序中引发问题。为解决此问题，GNU引入了嵌套函数（Nested Functions）扩展，允许在块作用域内定义函数，直接访问本地数据，避免使用全局变量。嵌套函数具有常规函数的外观和行为，能够解决数据共享问题，且无需额外的用户数据指针。然而，由于安全问题和历史原因，该特性未被广泛采用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言中函数指针和语言设计上的问题

不同观点：
• JonChesterfield对通过函数指针传递数据的方式持怀疑态度。他认为，C函数中不使用第二个数据指针参数（如在qsort_r等函数中引入的解决方案）是一个众所周知的经典问题，且这个问题已经存在几十年。他暗示这类问题早已有解决方案，如qsort_r，因此对新的类似解决方案的必要性表示怀疑。

• JonChesterfield提到C语言的多个设计缺陷，特别指出C语言不支持多值返回，这是一个让他特别困扰的问题。他认为这个限制会导致开发者不得不将多个值包装在结构体中，增加了不必要的复杂性。

• 关于函数与闭包的选择问题，JonChesterfield认为显式选择使用函数还是闭包并不重要，暗示这可能不是一个显著的问题或改进点。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了qsort_r等函数作为历史上的解决方案，指出了C语言在解决函数指针问题上的演变。
• 争议的焦点可能在于，是否真的有必要引入新的语言特性或函数设计来解决已存在已知解决方案的经典问题。
• JonChesterfield对C语言的某些设计缺陷（如不支持多值返回）表现出明显的不满，认为这些是更深层次的问题，相较之下，函数和闭包的选择问题显得不那么重要。

There were multiple limiting factors in getting data into the function outside of using
static

compare

main

This was, unfortunately, both bug-generating and limiting due to the data sharing issues. Concerns and problems around sharing data only grew in time as each program had to manage larger and larger swaths of 1980’s-style global variable soups, something that has famously ended up being used as a sign of negative code quality in legal matters. When global variables became more discouraged towards C95 and C99 to prevent unintended data clobbering or sharing, a new extension was cooked up by GCC to handle this program. Similar to an Ada feature but spun directly for C at the time, it was a feature lovingly dubbed Nested Functions.

data.title: Breaking Git with a carriage return and cloning RCE
data.author: dgl
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了CVE-2025-48384漏洞，该漏洞存在于Git中，当用户在Unix类平台上使用`git clone --recursive`命令克隆包含恶意代码的仓库时，可能导致远程代码执行。漏洞的根源在于Git配置文件中对回车符（CR）和换行符（LF）的处理不当。具体而言，Git在读取`.gitmodules`文件时，如果遇到CR字符，可能会错误地处理路径，导致控制字符被注入到文件名中，从而引发安全问题。攻击者可以利用此漏洞构造恶意的子模块路径，最终在克隆过程中执行任意代码。建议用户更新到修复版本的Git以防止此漏洞被利用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git子模块和钩子中的安全漏洞及其影响

不同观点：
• armchairhacker质疑该漏洞是否真的构成“远程代码执行（RCE）”，并询问其安全严重性。随后指出该漏洞允许恶意仓库通过Git钩子在克隆过程中执行代码，即使通常这些钩子不会在克隆时安装。
• 10000truths从配置文件使用自定义DSL的角度出发，指出由于缺乏正式的语法规范，解析器和序列化实现容易出现不同步，导致潜在漏洞。建议应有唯一的事实来源，并由此生成所有依赖项。
• acheong08成功复现了该问题，并提到其Git版本未更新，同时担心大多数用户可能需要很长时间才能升级。
• JdeBP通过引用历史文献讨论了该问题的历史背景，指出这类解析和引用问题早在20世纪末就被分析过，但至今仍然存在，强调需要反复吸取教训。
• capitol_对Git版本发布时间线感到困惑，指出多个发行版尚未修复该漏洞，并质疑Git是否回溯了发布日期。
• deanc担心Homebrew是否会受到该漏洞影响，尤其是它是否执行递归克隆，并提供了相关代码链接以供参考。
• Lockal质疑Git为何不使用Linux的Landlock机制来限制权限，并指出在每次漏洞演示中都能轻易触发恶意行为。
• tempodox认为一些不起眼的细节往往会导致严重后果。
• mrheosuper幽默地指出在2025年仍然没有解决使用不同换行符的问题。
• lossolo确认Homebrew和Debian Bookworm仍提供存在漏洞的Git版本。
• therealmarv表示需要等待Git更新。
• smaudet抱怨博客字体看起来眼睛疲劳。
• b0a04gl质疑Git为何在克隆过程中运行子模块钩子，认为在从未审计过的远程仓库克隆时运行钩子是非常危险的行为。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该漏洞是否构成“远程代码执行”以及其严重性。
• 对Git版本发布和更新的滞后性存在担忧，多个发行版和包管理器尚未提供修复。
• 对Git克隆过程中运行子模块钩子的设计决策提出质疑，认为存在安全隐患。
• 从历史和技术角度分析了该问题的根源和可能的解决办法。

44502330.article_content:
CVE-2025-48384: Breaking Git with a carriage return and cloning RCE
tl;dr:
On Unix-like platforms, if you use
git clone --recursive
on an
untrusted repo, it could achieve remote code execution. Update to a
fixed
version
of Git and other software that embeds Git (including GitHub Desktop).
If you've ever used an old mechanical typewriter, you know that when you get to
the end of the line there's a physical action to to get back to the start of
the line. Sometimes this was done through an actual lever on the typewriter,
later models had a button. Because this action — the
carriage
return
— was distinct from the
line feed, it has its own character. In ASCII this is the character known as
"Carriage Return", represented as "␍", character number 13. The "↵" icon, as
often seen on the "Enter" or "Return" key on a modern keyboard encodes this
action, along with the action of moving to the next line, known as "Line Feed"
(␊).
An Olympia SM9 with a carriage return lever. Via
classictypewriter.com
.
This legacy from the very early days of communications (carriage return was
introduced by the
Murray
code
in 1901!) is still
something we have to deal with. Unix attempted to simplify this by using just
LF (a "\n" in C-string terms) to separate lines, but Windows and various
Internet protocols use both CR+LF (a "\r\n" in C-string terms).
Why am I talking about
this
?
git has a simple .ini style configuration format, that looks like this:
[section]
key = value
If this was just used in the user’s configuration files there wouldn’t be a
concern about the formats that are accepted. However this configuration format
is also used in the
.gitmodules
file, which is a file that is checked into
the git repository that tracks submodules.
The format supports DOS line endings. It handles this in the fairly obvious way
of stripping them when it reads lines, below is the function get_next_char in
config.c:
static int get_next_char(struct config_source *cs)
{
int c = cs->do_fgetc(cs);
if (c == '\r') {
/* DOS like systems */
c = cs->do_fgetc(cs);
if (c != '\n') {
if (c != EOF)
cs->do_ungetc(c, cs);
c = '\r';
}
}
The
cs->do_fgetc
call is nearly equivalent to the standard C function
fgetc()
, so even without knowledge of git's particular functions this is
quite understandable.
It boils down to: If the character is a carriage return (
\r
), then look at
the next character, if it is a line feed (
\n
), just return a line feed (and
eat the carriage return). If however the next character isn’t a line feed,
return a carriage return (
\r
) and put the next character back (
ungetc
), so
it is returned next time.
The key thing to understand here is that this is done per line. So if for some
reason a line happens to end with a CR, it will be stripped, regardless of the
overall format of the file.
In addition to the code to read the configuration, git can also write
configuration files, for example when the user uses
git config
to set a
configuration value, it will use the code below to write
key = value
pairs
out to the file.
static ssize_t write_pair(int fd, const char *key, const char *value, [...]
{
[...]
/*
* Check to see if the value needs to be surrounded with a dq pair.
* Note that problematic characters are always backslash-quoted; this
* check is about not losing leading or trailing SP and strings that
* follow beginning-of-comment characters (i.e. ';' and '#') by the
* configuration parser.
*/
if (value[0] == ' ')
quote = "\"";
for (i = 0; value[i]; i++)
if (value[i] == ';' || value[i] == '#')
quote = "\"";
if (i && value[i - 1] == ' ')
quote = "\"";
strbuf_addf(&sb, "\t%s = %s", key + store->baselen + 1, quote);
The actual bug is in the interaction of the above get_next_char function with
this code. Elsewhere in the configuration reading code git supports quoted
strings, using double quotes. However, when it writes a value back out to the
configuration file, it will quote it only if it contains spaces in certain
positions, or a
;
or
#
anywhere. This means when it later reads the value
write_pair
wrote to the configuration file back, it can be tricked to drop a
final
\r
off the value.
So, if we have a file with
key = "foo^M"
, when it's written out again it
becomes
key = foo^M
(where
^M
is the literal CR character).
As I alluded to already,
.gitmodules
is untrusted, so if we can confuse the
config parser, maybe that’s enough to confuse the code that handles submodules
within git?
On Unix based systems (not Windows), it is possible to have control characters
in filenames, so a path entry like the following in
.gitmodules
will attempt
to check out the module into a directory named with a control character in its
name.
[submodule "foo"]
path = "foo^M"
However when this is written out by git’s configuration code to
.git/modules/foo/config
, it will look something like this:
[core]
workdir = ../../../foo^M
The validation has already happened against the untrusted path that was read
from
.gitmodules
. This means the path then essentially changes

data.title: Dynamical origin of Theia, the last giant impactor on Earth
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 本文通过行星形成动力学模拟，探讨了地球最后巨型撞击体Theia的起源。模拟从类地行星胚胎和星子环开始，并包括木星内移的碳质（CC）星子和胚胎。结果显示，该情景能符合多个约束条件，包括类地行星的质量和轨道、地球的CC质量比例、火星较低的CC比例（仅从星子获得）、月球形成撞击的时间以及后期以非碳质体为主的吸积阶段。为使模拟成立，散布的CC物体总质量需为0.2-0.3地球质量，胚胎与星子质量比至少为8，CC胚胎质量在0.01-0.05地球质量之间。模拟表明，Theia有约50%的概率是碳质物体，支持了宇宙化学研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于地球历史上的巨型撞击事件及其可能的物理和生物影响

不同观点：
• [nehal3m] 提到最近一次巨大的撞击事件，暗示这是迄今为止最后一次此类事件，但没有展开具体分析。
• [shadowgovt] 对该理论进行解释，认为该假设（5-10%的地球质量来自一次碳质巨型撞击）是有价值的，因为它并没有与当前对太阳系形成的理解相矛盾。该评论强调通过模拟验证假设的重要性。
• [readthenotes1] 提到月球的质量仅为地球的1.2%，因此即便有巨大撞击，地球的质量增长也是有限的，对“地球被显著增大的可能性”提出质疑。

补充讨论：
• [echelon] 提出一种假设情景：如果在撞击事件前，地球或Theia上已经存在生命，尤其是智慧生命，目睹了这一灾难性事件。该评论进一步探讨了智慧生命演化的时间尺度问题，认为这种情景虽然不现实，但具有想象空间。
• 该评论还引申讨论了宇宙大爆炸后早期宇宙温度适于生命产生的可能性，提出生命可能直接在太空中形成，并通过原始的“生命汤”传播到整个宇宙。这一观点将讨论引向了更广泛的宇宙生命起源问题。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于巨型撞击事件对地球质量的实际影响，以及这种假设是否与当前的天文学和物理学知识相矛盾。[shadowgovt]认为假设值得探讨，而[readthenotes1]则质疑地球质量的显著增长。
• [echelon]的评论引发了关于生命在撞击事件前是否可能存在的想象性讨论，虽然科学上不被广泛接受，但提出了一个有趣的哲学和科学假设。

(astro-ph)

Title:
Dynamical origin of Theia, the last giant impactor on Earth
Authors:
Duarte Branco
,
Sean N. Raymond
,
Pedro Machado
View a PDF of the paper titled Dynamical origin of Theia, the last giant impactor on Earth, by Duarte Branco and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Cosmochemical studies have proposed that Earth accreted roughly 5-10% of its mass from carbonaceous (CC) material, with a large fraction delivered late via its final impactor, Theia (the Moon-forming impactor). Here, we evaluate this idea using dynamical simulations of terrestrial planet formation, starting from a standard setup with a population of planetary embryos and planetesimals laid out in a ring centered between Venus and Earth's orbits, and also including a population of CC planetesimals and planetary embryos scattered inward by Jupiter. We find that this scenario can match a large number of constraints, including i) the terrestrial planets' masses and orbits; ii) the CC mass fraction of Earth; iii) the much lower CC mass fraction of Mars, as long as Mars only accreted CC planetesimals (but no CC embryos); iv) the timing of the last giant (Moon-forming) impact; and v) a late accretion phase dominated by non-carbonaceous (NC) bodies. For this scenario to work, the total mass in scattered CC objects must have been ~ 0.2 - 0.3 M$_{\oplus}$ , with an embryo-to-planetesimal mass ratio of at least 8, and CC embryos in the ~ 0.01 - 0.05 M$_{\oplus}$ mass range. In that case, our simulations show there are roughly 50-50 odds of Earth's last giant impactor (Theia) having been a carbonaceous object - either a pure CC embryo or an NC embryo that previously accreted a CC embryo. Our simulations thus provide dynamical validation of cosmochemical studies.

data.title: New Horizons images enable first test of interstellar navigation
data.author: jnord
data.article_summary: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft, currently traveling through the Kuiper Belt, has been used for the first demonstration of interstellar navigation by astronomers. Due to its distant location, stars like Proxima Centauri and Wolf 359 appear in different positions compared to Earth's view, creating a parallax effect. Scientists, led by Tod Lauer, utilized this effect and data from the Gaia space telescope to determine New Horizons' position in the galaxy. Although less accurate than NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN), this method could improve with better equipment and offers advantages for deep space navigation, as it does not rely on signals from Earth. However, its practical use is limited until future interstellar missions are planned.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对New Horizons探测器导航方法的准确性及新技术应用的评价，以及对NewScientist订阅的咨询。

不同观点：
• [aerospades] 认为视差法的准确性较低，只能将New Horizons定位在一个半径为6000万公里的球体内，相比之下，NASA的SEXTANT任务通过脉冲星导航将误差控制在约10公里，并且在星际空间中仍然有效。尽管视差法不如脉冲星导航精确，但认为这种创新仍然值得称赞，因为New Horizons是2006年发射的，显示了老技术的新应用。

• [xlii] 对NewScientist杂志表示兴趣，询问其他人对订阅该杂志的意见，这属于对信息源的信任度和价值评估问题，而非直接讨论技术问题。

补充讨论：
• [aerospades] 提供了具体的数据对比，视差法的误差范围（半径6000万公里）和脉冲星导航的误差范围（约10公里），通过数据支持其认为脉冲星导航更精确的观点。

• [xlii] 的评论属于题外询问，显示出对信息来源的关注，可能影响对相关科技新闻的获取和信任程度。

争议焦点：
• 视差法与脉冲星导航的准确性比较是讨论的核心争议点。[aerospades] 明确指出了两种方法在精度上的显著差异，但同时也承认视差法在老技术上的创新应用价值。

总结：评论中既有对新技术（脉冲星导航）精确性的肯定，也有对老技术（视差法）创新使用的赞赏，同时还涉及对科技信息来源（NewScientist杂志）的信任和订阅咨询。

44484557.article_content:
Artist’s illustration of NASA’s New Horizons spacecraft in the outer solar system
Joe Olmsted/STScI
As it hurtles out of our solar system, NASA’s
New Horizons
spacecraft is so far from Earth that the stars in the Milky Way appear in markedly different positions compared with our own view. Astronomers have now used this change in perspective to work out the probe’s position in the galaxy, in the first ever example of interstellar navigation.
New Horizons was launched in 2006, initially to
study Pluto
, but it has since travelled way beyond this point, ploughing on through the Kuiper belt, a vast, wide band of rocks and dust billions of miles from the sun. It is now speeding at tens of thousands of kilometres per hour.
Read more
This mind-blowing map shows Earth’s position within the vast universe
Advertisement
When gazing at the night sky from Earth, the stars are so far away that they don’t appear to change positions when viewed from different locations, unless you have a powerful telescope. But from New Horizons’ viewpoint, there is a significant change in star positions due to the parallax effect. This was
demonstrated
in 2020 when the probe beamed back pictures of two nearby stars, Proxima Centauri and Wolf 359, to Earth.
Now,
Tod Lauer
at the US National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory in Arizona and his colleagues have used this effect to work out the position of New Horizons. They did it by comparing the probe’s photos of Proxima Centauri and Wolf 359 with measurements from the Gaia space telescope, which has produced the most detailed map of stars in our Milky Way.
“We have a good enough three-dimensional map of the galaxy around us that you can find out where you are,” says Lauer. “It’s a remarkable accuracy, with your own camera [on board a spacecraft].”
Free newsletter
Sign up to Launchpad
Bring the galaxy to your inbox every month, with the latest space news, launches and astronomical occurrences from New Scientist’s Leah Crane.
Sign up to newsletter
To calculate the spacecraft’s position, he and his team looked at the position of the stars as they appeared from New Horizons’ on-board camera, drawing a line of sight back from both stars and working out where the two lines were closest. Then, they used the precise position of both stars from Gaia’s star map to work out where this point was in relation to the solar system.
This two-frame animation shows the shifting position of Proxima Centauri as viewed from Earth and New Horizons
Almost all spacecraft calculate their bearings to within tens of metres using NASA’s Deep Space Network (DSN), a collection of radio transmitters on Earth that send regular signals out to space. In comparison, the parallax method was far less accurate, locating New Horizons within a sphere with a radius of 60 million kilometres, about half the distance between Earth and the sun.
“We’re not going to put the Deep Space Network out of business – this is only a demo proof of concept,” says Lauer. However, with a better camera and equipment they could improve the accuracy by up to 100 times, he says.
Read more
Why we must investigate Phobos, the solar system's strangest object
Using this technique for interstellar navigation could offer advantages over the DSN because it could give more accurate location readings as a spacecraft gets further away from Earth, as well as being able to operate autonomously without needing to wait for a radio signal to come from our solar system, says
Massimiliano Vasile
at the University of Strathclyde, UK.
“If you travel to an actual star, we are talking about light years,” says Vasile. “What happens is that your signal from the Deep Space Network has to travel all the way there and then all the way back, and it’s travelling at the speed of light, so it takes years.”
However, there are no missions in the works to go deep into interstellar space by any agency, says Vasile, so the utility of this particular technique is limited until one takes shape, he says.

data.title: Blind to Disruption – The CEOs Who Missed the Future
data.author: ArmageddonIt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要讲述了美国20世纪初的马车制造商如何面对汽车这一颠覆性技术的冲击。在汽车出现之前，美国有超过4000家马车和货车制造商，但随着汽车的普及，这些公司逐渐被淘汰，最终只有一家幸存。文章引用海明威的话来比喻企业如何在不知不觉中走向破产：先是缓慢衰落，然后突然崩溃。文章强调，面对颠覆性技术，企业领导者必须适应变化，否则将面临淘汰。文章以历史为例，警示现代企业必须时刻警惕行业变革和创新技术的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术的发展、应用及其对企业和社会的潜在影响

不同观点：
• jampa：认为AI应用早已存在，当前的AI热潮只是让这些技术变得更易访问，但过度关注前端的ChatGPT式应用是错误的。AI应在幕后赋能用户，而不是成为表面上的噱头。
• danbruc：对当前的AI模型持怀疑态度，认为大型语言模型最终会成为一种更简单和易访问的用户界面，但它们有根本的局限性，未来的AI还需要新的突破。
• BrenBarn：关注AI带来的道德和伦理问题，如隐私、创造力、著作权和不平等，认为这些问题比市场变化更为重要。
• barrysaunders：指出过去许多公司因追逐技术潮流而失败，认为预测未来是困难的，不能简单地用历史类比来判断AI的未来。
• kylecazar：批评当前企业过度追逐AI技术而忽视基础，认为应回归 fundamentals。
• johncole：认为AI hype与 carriage公司未能转型的情况不同，现代CEO有明确的动机去制造 hype。

data.title: Thunderbird 140 “Eclipse”
data.author: TangerineDream
data.article_summary: Thunderbird 140 "Eclipse" 已发布，作为最新的扩展支持版本，它在之前版本基础上引入了多项新功能和改进。包括自适应黑暗消息模式，可在暗模式下自动调整消息显示；增强的外观设置，允许用户轻松自定义界面；原生操作系统通知，支持快速操作邮件；以及简化的账户中心，方便用户快速添加和管理多账户。此外，还支持手动文件夹排序、实验性Exchange支持、生成QR码以便于移动端设置等功能。尽管可能存在一些问题，用户可以通过手动或等待自动更新来升级至Thunderbird 140。该版本适用于Windows、Linux和MacOS。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Thunderbird电子邮件客户端的评价和功能改进建议，包括其长期存在的bug、功能缺陷、UI问题以及新功能的需求。

不同观点：
• 一些用户对Thunderbird的一个长达17年未修复的bug表示严重不满，该bug会导致邮件数据被删除。用户质疑为什么如此严重的问题没有被优先解决。[fouronnes3]
• 另一位用户throwaway81523详细列举了Thunderbird的多项功能缺陷，包括搜索系统在大邮件量下的崩溃、地址簿的排序问题、自动创建的存档文件夹排序不合理等，并认为在基本功能完善之前不应添加新功能。
• 对于UI设计，piskov对用户使用抽象图片而不是实际截图表示疑惑，没有深入讨论功能问题。
• 部分用户关注Thunderbird在系统托盘图标和通知功能上的不足，并讨论了替代方案如Betterbird和birdtray。[AdmiralAsshat, nticompass]
• 用户mvdwoord分享了从Thunderbird转向Google和Office 365的经历，强调Thunderbird在与其他系统如Outlook的整合上存在不足，特别是日历和同步功能，但仍希望有一个开源的统一解决方案。
• 一些用户如yakattak和Davidbrcz对Thunderbird的改进表示欢迎，特别是黑暗模式和新的帐户管理功能，并鼓励其他用户尝试。[yakattak, Davidbrcz]
• 用户CoolChum指出Thunderbird缺乏设置同步功能，导致在多台PC上使用不便，并批评其最近的UI改动模仿Windows 11的上下文菜单，无法还原。
• 用户mr_tox认为Thunderbird仍是OSX上最好的邮件客户端，但未详细展开。
• 用户Tepix在升级到版本140后遇到了新帐户添加失败的问题，对新版本的稳定性表示失望。
• 用户roflmaostc提到Thunderbird在某些窗口管理器下界面显示异常的问题，怀疑是与特定WM配置有关。
• 最后，用户XorNot关心Oauth和Yubikey支持问题，特别是与O365和Okta的整合，希望Thunderbird能改进对此类认证方案的支持。

补充讨论：
• Thunderbird的长期bug和功能缺陷是用户最主要的抱怨点，尤其是数据丢失问题。
• 用户对多PC环境下的设置同步功能有强烈需求。
• 新功能如黑暗模式和帐户管理改进受到部分用户欢迎，但新版本的稳定性受到质疑。
• 系统托盘图标和Oauth认证支持也是用户关注的焦点。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于Thunderbird开发团队为何没有优先修复严重的数据丢失bug，而是不断添加新功能或改变UI。

Welcome to Thunderbird 140 “Eclipse”
July 7, 2025
Monica Ayhens-Madon
0		responses
The wait is over! Thunderbird 140 “Eclipse” has reached totality. From all of us at the Thunderbird project, from MZLA staff and the Thunderbird Council to our global community of contributors, we’re excited to announce the latest Extended Support Release has arrived.
Eclipse not only builds on Thunderbird 128 “Nebula,” but also the recent features and improvements from the
Monthly Release channel
. This latest release transforms your email experience with adaptive dark messaging and improved visual controls. Enhanced features keep everyday email tasks light and effortless, while the streamlined new Account Hub ensures adding new accounts is a snap.
Dark Message Mode
Thunderbird’s Dark Mode now automatically adapts your messages when enabled, to ensure your Dark Mode experience stays totally dark. Need to bring your messages back into the light in case of visual problems? Adjust your message view as needed with a quick optional toggle.
Appearance Settings
Make Thunderbird yours across all your folders and accounts with a single click in the Settings (panel). Change your message list layout between Cards and Table view, adjust your Cards View, and set your default sorting order and threading options with ease.
Native OS Notifications
Leverage the speed and ease of your Operating System’s built-in notifications, whether you’re on Windows, Linux, or Mac. Quickly delete, archive, or use customizable actions directly from your notifications and get more done with your day.
Account Hub
Adding a new account to Thunderbird is now easier than ever. Connect all of your emails, address books and calendars in a few easy steps.
Manual Folder Sorting
Don’t like the order for your custom folders? Just click and drag to arrange them exactly how you want.
Don’t like the order for your custom folders? Just click and drag to arrange them exactly how you want.
More Refinements & Updates
Experimental Exchange Support
Natively set up a Microsoft Exchange account in Thunderbird by enabling a preference.
Export for Mobile
Generate a QR code to quickly transfer your account settings and credentials to your Thunderbird for Android app.
Horizontal Scroll for Table View
Lots of tabular data? Let the message list scroll horizontally, like a spreadsheet or file manager.
Bug Fixes and Improvements
Thousands of bug fixes and performance improvements to bring you the smooth, reliable Thunderbird experience you expect.
Looking Forward
Whether you’re waiting for the next Thunderbird ESR or total solar eclipse, we understand that sometimes you want new features, or that cosmic awe, sooner. While we can’t change the universe, you can now get the latest Thunderbird features as they land, instead of once a year.
Switch to Thunderbird Release
and enjoy monthly updates with the same dependable stability.

data.article_summary: BreakerMachines 是一个为 Ruby 和 Rails 设计的现代电路断路器库，具有线程安全、支持异步和纤维（fiber）、内置回退机制、高效内存使用和监控等特点。它基于 state_machines 构建，支持对分布式系统的保护，防止级联故障。该库提供对冲请求、多后端支持、百分比阈值、动态断路器和丰富的回调与检测功能。此外，它还集成了 ActiveSupport::Notifications，并提供详细的文档和多种测试指南。BreakerMachines 旨在解决微服务架构中的常见问题，如过度重试导致的自我 DDoS 攻击，帮助开发者构建更健壮的系统。

主要讨论点：关于电路断路器（circuit breaker）和令牌桶（token bucket）机制在系统保护中的使用及其文档编写的反馈

• [seuros] 作为项目作者，介绍了BreakerMachines的特点和设计目标，强调其在处理生产环境中连锁故障的优势。他列举了项目的多个关键功能，如真正的异步支持、内置回退机制、线程安全等，并指出电路断路器在保护应用免受外部API故障影响方面的重要性。他还提到未来计划增加并行功能，并寻求对API设计和潜在边缘案例的反馈。

总结：讨论涉及电路断路器和令牌桶机制的比较，以及项目文档编写的反馈，焦点在于两者的适用性和文档编写质量。

Why I Open Sourced This

data.title: Cmdk – CD anywhere and open anything in your terminal
data.author: mieubrisse
data.article_summary: "cmdk" 是一个终端工具，通过类似 Notion、Slack 的 ⌘-K 快捷键，帮助用户快速访问文件系统中的任何文件或目录。用户无需反复使用 `cd` 和 `ls` 命令，只需输入 `cmdk` 或绑定 ⌘-K 快捷键，即可开始搜索并预览文件。目录将被直接进入，文本文件在 vim 中打开，图片和 PDF 则在预览应用中打开，`.key` 文件在 Keynote 中打开。该工具依赖于 `fzf`，并提供了多种快捷操作如多选文件、清除选择等。此外，某些系统目录如 `Library` 和 `/` 的内容默认被排除，需两次访问才能查看。未来计划包括自定义打开程序、收藏文件和存储历史记录等功能。
data.comments_summary:

• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 引用了 ⌘+K 作为在Terminal中的一种快捷操作，但没有进一步解释具体如何使用或其潜在问题。此外，他的评论后半部分似乎与主要讨论点无关，提到“Nitrous oxide是赛车界的甘油”，这可能是一种类比或幽默插入。

cmdk
The ⌘-k "access anything" shortcut is awesome on Notion, Slack, etc.
The terminal, by comparison, is a dinosaur: tons of repeated
cd
and
ls
and
TAB
just to get anywhere.
This is ⌘-k for the terminal: access anything on your filesystem, from anywhere, with previews before you open:
When you press enter...
Directories get
cd
d to
Text files get opened in
vim
Images and PDFs get opened in the Preview app
.key
files get opened in Keynote
I'm extremely grateful to
fzf
; this project wouldn't be possible without it. I'd been fed up with terminal navigation for a decade, and fzf was the missing piece needed to make cmdk possible.
Installation
Install
cmdk
and dependencies:
#
NOTE: bat, tiv, and poppler are optional: for previewing text, image, and PDF files respectively
brew install fzf fd bat tiv poppler
git clone git@github.com:mieubrisse/cmdk.git
~
/.cmdk
Add to your
.zshrc
or
.bashrc
:
source
~
/.cmdk/cmdk.sh
#
This will make a 'cmdk' function available in your shell
(Optional) Bind the
⌘-k
hotkey to send the text
cmdk\n
in your terminal
💡 In iTerm, this is done with
Settings → Profiles → Keys → Keybindings → + → Send Text
, then binding
⌘-k
to send the text
cmdk\n
.
💡 If you prefer another hotkey (e.g.
⌘-p
), simply bind that to send the
cmdk\n
string instead.
Open a new shell and press ⌘-K (if you bound it) or enter
cmdk
(if you don't bind ⌘-K)
Usage
Press ⌘-k (or type
cmdk
) and...
Type to start filtering
💡 If you're trying to get a directory, add a
/
to the end of your search term. E.g.
down/
will pull up the
Downloads
directory
Ctrl-j
and
Ctrl-k
to scroll up and down the results list
ENTER
to select the result
TAB
to select multiple items before
ENTER
Ctrl-u
to clear the selection
⚠️
Some directories like
Library
,
/
, and
.git
are full of stuff users don't need to access, so their contents are excluded. To get to their contents, first ⌘-k to them and then ⌘-k again to see their contents.
💡 Sometimes you only want to jump to the contents of the current directory. This can be done by calling
cmdk -o
. I've set up a separate iTerm hotkey for this:
⌘-l
to send
cmdk -o\n
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Grok模型的性能、可用性、技术细节及争议

不同观点：
• **关于"flag"功能的问题：**
  - [MangoToupe] 认为"flag"功能存在问题，导致被标记的评论无法显示，影响了对话的完整性。他们希望可以禁用该功能以查看和参与被标记的评论。

• **关于Grok模型性能的评价：**
  - [modeless] 指出Grok在新基准测试中表现优异，超越了其他模型如o3、Gemini和Claude。
  - [tibbar] 对Grok Heavy的多代理并行运行策略表示赞赏，认为这是合理的技术进步，尽管成本高且速度慢。
  - [rpozarickij] 认为Grok的语音模式有待改进，特别是在自动turn检测方面，但对其支持小语种表示肯定。
  - [raspasov] 强调Grok在深度研究中的优越表现，并对Grok 4充满期待。

• **关于Grok的实际应用和可访问性：**
  - [lexandstuff] 质疑Grok的实际应用情况，认为其需要更强大的模型才能吸引用户。
  - [sidcool] 关心新模型的用户可用性。
  - [simianwords] 提到获取Grok 4 Heavy的困难和高成本问题。

• **关于Grok的争议：**
  - [archagon] 指出Grok近期涉及的反犹太主义问题被掩盖，认为这是不负责任的表现，并批评公司缺乏道歉和安全措施。
  - [jppope] 认为尽管Elon Musk最近使用了一些噱头，但在这个领域仍有潜力，尤其是在拥有合适人才的情况下。

• **关于技术细节和基准测试成绩的讨论：**
  - [TheAceOfHearts] 请求用户测试Grok 4在简单文字搜索问题上的表现。
  - [porphyra] 对Grok在Humanity's Last Exam上的高分表示惊讶，并与其他模型进行对比。

补充讨论：
- 一些用户对Grok的实际应用和可访问性表示关注，尤其是在集成和高成本方面。
- 有用户质疑Grok的商业决策和领导层问题，如Elon Musk与OpenAI的关系。
- 争议焦点在于Grok模型的技术表现与伦理问题，特别是近期涉及的反犹太主义事件。

data.title: Browser hijacking campaign infects 2.3M Chrome, Edge users
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 一篇报道披露了一场大规模浏览器劫持活动，名为RedDirection，影响了超过230万Chrome和Edge用户。这些恶意扩展程序最初功能正常，如颜色选择器、表情符号键盘等，并拥有Google的验证徽章，因此用户信任。然而，经过版本更新，这些扩展被注入恶意代码，秘密监控用户浏览活动，并将数据发送到攻击者服务器。最危险的是，这些更新通过浏览器自动安装，无需用户操作。研究人员警告，用户应立即卸载相关扩展并监控账户异常活动。受影响扩展包括Geco颜色选择器等18个，涉及VPN代理、天气预报、视频速度控制等功能。

44518620.article_content:
Research
24
Massive browser hijacking campaign infects 2.3M Chrome, Edge users
24
These extensions weren't malware-laced from the start, researcher says
Jessica Lyons
Tue 8 Jul 2025
//
19:07 UTC
A Chrome and Edge extension with more than 100,000 downloads that displays Google's verified badge does what it purports to do: It delivers a color picker to users. Unfortunately, it also hijacks every browser session, tracks activities across websites, and backdoors victims' web browsers, according to Koi Security researchers.
Color pickers let users select any color from a website and copy it into a clipboard for later use - helpful for designing apps, websites, and the like. This particular extension from Geco is still available for download via both
Microsoft's
and
Google's
respective stores at press time. Neither company responded to
The Register
's inquiries, but we will update this story if that changes.
The Geco extension has more than 800 reviews on the Chrome Web Store, 4.2 stars (out of 5), and "featured" placement. Microsoft's Edge Add-ons shows similarly glowing write-ups from its 1,000-plus users, and it looks like a perfectly safe extension.
"This isn't some obvious scam extension thrown together in a weekend,"
said
Koi Security analyst Idan Dardikman in a Tuesday blog. "This is a carefully crafted Trojan horse."
The Register
also reached out to the developer for comment but did not receive a response.
The Geco color picker, according to Koi Security, is "just the tip of the iceberg," and part of a much larger browser-hijacking campaign dubbed RedDirection. The campaign consists of 18 malicious extensions spanning both Chrome and Edge stores that all share the same snooping capabilities. All 18 extensions are listed at the bottom of this story.
"Combined, these eighteen extensions have infected over 2.3 million users across both browsers, creating one of the largest browser hijacking operations we've documented," Dardikman wrote.
Netflix, Apple, BofA websites hijacked with fake help-desk numbers
Sneaky SnakeKeylogger slithers into Windows inboxes to steal sensitive secrets
Chrome users – get an alert when extensions are in danger of falling into wrong hands
Suspected Scattered Spider domains target everyone from manufacturers to Chipotle
The extensions offer all sorts of capabilities: emoji keyboards, weather forecasts, video speed controllers, VPN proxies for Discord and TikTok, dark themes, volume boosters, and YouTube unblockers (useful if your employer, school, or government blocks the popular video site). But in addition to providing these legitimate functions, they secretly surveil users' web browsing activity, capturing URLs, sending this info to a remote attacker-controlled server along with the victim's unique tracking ID, and even redirecting people's browsers if instructed, according to the researchers.
What makes this even sneakier — and likely explains the Google verified badge — is that these extensions weren't laced with malware from the start.
According to Dardikman, the code started out clean and sometimes remained that way for years before the malware was introduced during version updates. "Due to how Google and Microsoft handle browser extension updates, these malicious versions auto-installed silently for over 2.3 million users across both platforms, most of whom never clicked anything," he said.
If you've installed any of the extensions listed below, uninstall now, clear your browser data, and keep an eye on your accounts for any suspicious activity.

Async Ruby is the Future of AI Apps (And It's Already Here)
Carmine Paolino
Jul 9, 2025
After a decade as an ML engineer/scientist immersed in Python’s async ecosystem, returning to Ruby felt like stepping back in time. Where was the async revolution? Why was everyone still using threads for everything? SolidQueue, Sidekiq, GoodJob – all thread-based. Even newer solutions defaulted to the same concurrency model.
Coming from Python, where the entire community had reorganized around
asyncio
, this seemed bizarre. FastAPI replaced Flask. Every library spawned an async twin. The transformation was total and necessary.
Then, building
RubyLLM
and
Chat with Work
, I noticed that
LLM communication is async Ruby’s killer app
. The unique demands of streaming AI responses – long-lived connections, token-by-token delivery, thousands of concurrent conversations – expose exactly why async matters.
Here’s the exciting bit: once I understood Ruby’s approach to async, I realized it’s actually
superior
to Python’s. While Python forced everyone to rewrite their entire stack, Ruby quietly built something better. Your existing code just works. No syntax changes. No library migrations. Just better performance when you need it.
The async ecosystem that
Samuel Williams
and others have been building for years suddenly makes perfect sense. We just needed the right use case to see it.
Why LLM Communication Breaks Everything
LLM applications create a perfect storm of challenges that expose every weakness in thread-based concurrency:
1. Slot Starvation
Configure any thread-based job queue with 25 workers:
class
StreamAIResponseJob
<
ApplicationJob
def
perform
(
chat
,
message
)
# This job occupies 1 of your 25 slots...
chat
.
ask
(
message
)
do
|
chunk
|
# ...for the ENTIRE streaming duration (30-60 seconds)
broadcast_chunk
(
chunk
)
# Thread is 99% idle, just waiting for tokens
end
# Slot only freed here, after full response
end
end
Your 26th user? They’re waiting in line. Not because your server is busy, but because all your workers are occupied by jobs waiting for tokens.
2. Resource Multiplication
Each thread needs its own:
Database connection (25 threads = 25 connections minimum)
Stack memory allocation
OS thread management overhead
For 1000 concurrent conversations, you’d need 1000 threads. Each thread needs its database connection. That’s 1000 database connections for threads that are 99% idle.
3. Performance Overhead
Real benchmarks show
1
:
Creating a thread: ~80μs
Thread context switch: ~1.3μs
Maximum throughput: ~5,000 requests/second
When you’re handling thousands of streaming connections, these microseconds add up to real latency.
4. Scalability Challenges
Try creating 10,000 threads and the OS scheduler starts to struggle. The overhead becomes crushing. Yet modern AI apps need to handle thousands of concurrent conversations.
These aren’t separate issues – they’re all symptoms of the same architectural mismatch. LLM communication is fundamentally different from traditional background jobs.
Understanding Concurrency: Threads vs Async
To understand why LLM applications are async’s perfect use case – and why Ruby’s implementation is so elegant – we need to build up from first principles.
The Hierarchy: Processes, Threads, and Fibers
Think of your computer as an office building:
Processes
are like separate offices – each with its own locked door, furniture, and files. They can’t see into each other’s spaces (memory isolation).
Threads
are like workers sharing the same office – they can access the same filing cabinets (shared memory) but need to coordinate to avoid collisions.
Fibers
are like multiple tasks juggled by one worker at their desk – switching between them manually when waiting for something (like a phone call).
Scheduling: The Core Difference
The fundamental question in concurrency is: who decides when to switch between tasks?
Threads: Preemptive Multitasking
With threads, the operating system is the boss. It forcibly interrupts running threads to give others a turn:

end
end
Each thread:
Gets scheduled by the OS kernel
Can be interrupted mid-execution (in Ruby, after 100ms)
Blocks individually on I/O operations
Requires OS resources and kernel data structures
Needs its own resources (like database connections)
Fibers: Cooperative Concurrency
With fibers, switching is voluntary – they only yield at I/O boundaries:

Elon Musk’s AI company, xAI, late on Wednesday released its latest flagship AI model, Grok 4, and unveiled a new $300-per-month AI subscription plan, SuperGrok Heavy.
Grok
is xAI’s answer to models like OpenAI’s
ChatGPT
and Google’s
Gemini
, and can analyze images and respond to questions. In recent months, Grok has become more deeply integrated into Musk’s social network, X, which
was recently acquired by xAI
. However, that has also put
Grok’s misbehavior front and center for millions of users
.
Introducing Grok 4, the world's most powerful AI model. Watch the livestream now:
https://t.co/59iDX5s2ck
— xAI (@xai)
July 10, 2025
The expectations are high for Grok 4. The latest AI model from xAI will be stacked up against OpenAI’s forthcoming AI model,
GPT-5,
which is expected to launch later this summer.
“With respect to academic questions, Grok 4 is better than PhD level in every subject, no exceptions,” said Elon Musk during a livestream Wednesday night. “At times, it may lack common sense, and it has not yet invented new technologies or discovered new physics, but that is just a matter of time.”
Musk wore a leather jacket and sat besides xAI leaders to launch Grok 4 (Credit: xAI)
The launch of Grok 4 comes amid a tumultuous week for Elon Musk’s companies. Earlier on Wednesday,
Linda Yaccarino stepped down
from her role as the CEO of X after roughly two years with the company. X has yet to announce her successor.
Yaccarino’s departure comes just days after Grok’s official, automated X account responded to users with
antisemitic comments criticizing Hollywood’s “Jewish executives” and praising Hitler.
xAI had to briefly limit Grok’s account and delete the offensive posts. In response to the incident, xAI appeared to have
removed a recently added section from Grok’s public system prompt
, a list of instructions for the AI chatbot to follow, that told it not to shy away from making “politically incorrect” claims.
Musk and xAI’s leaders largely avoided discussing the incident, instead focusing on Grok 4’s performance and capabilities.

xAI claims that Grok 4 shows frontier level performance on several benchmarks, including Humanity’s Last Exam— a challenging test measuring AI’s ability to answer thousands of crowdsourced questions on subjects like math, humanities, and natural science. According to xAI, Grok 4 scored 25.4% on Humanity’s Last Exam without “tools,” outperforming Google’s Gemini 2.5 Pro, which scored 21.6%, and OpenAI’s o3 (high), which scored 21%.
xAI claims that Grok 4 Heavy, with “tools,” was able to achieve a score of 44.4%, outperforming Gemini 2.5 Pro with tools, which scored 26.9%.
The nonprofit Arc Prize says that

on its ARC-AGI-2 test — another difficult benchmark that consists of puzzle-like problems where an AI has to identify visual patterns — scoring 16.2%. That’s nearly twice the score of the next best commercial AI model, Claude Opus 4.
Grok 4’s performance on several academic benchmarks (Credit: xAI)
Alongside Grok 4 and Grok 4 Heavy, xAI launched its most expensive AI subscription plan yet, a $300-per-month subscription called SuperGrok Heavy. Subscribers to the plan will get an early preview to Grok 4 Heavy, as well as early access to new features. The plan is similar to ultra-premium tiers offered by OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic, but xAI now offers the most expensive subscription among major AI providers.
SuperGrok Heavy subscribers may get early access to some new products xAI plans to launch in the coming months. The company said Wednesday that an AI coding model is coming in August, a multi-modal agent in September, and a video generation model in October.

data.title: Do AI Tutors Empower or Enslave Learners?
data.author: jruohonen
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人工智能（AI）在教育中的应用，特别是AI导师对学习者的影响。文章指出，尽管AI可以支持学习，但过度依赖可能导致认知能力下降、学习者自主性丧失、情感风险以及隐私问题。这种依赖还可能破坏有意义的学习过程，助长依赖性和 conformity（ conformity指从众行为），并削弱学生的自我效能感和学术诚信。为避免这些问题，文章建议对AI的使用应透明、有意识且批判性地进行，确保AI作为学习的支持工具而非认知捷径，从而真正赋能学习者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在教育中的角色，特别是作为“AI导师”的有效性和潜力，以及对现有教育问题的反思。

不同观点：
• [jjani] 认为文章标题提到的“AI导师”具有误导性。文章内容只是泛泛地讨论了学生如何使用AI，并没有具体涉及“导师”的概念。如果只是让人工智能代做作业，不能称之为“导师”行为。
• [jruohonen] 对文章中提到的“AI素养”持怀疑态度，认为文章引用的例子并不能有效支持其论点，且对AI在教育中的应用前景感到担忧。
• [spwa4] 指出文章对AI的批评并不针对AI独有的问题，而是与资金和努力相关的普遍教育问题。作者认为，尽管AI可能无法达到最优秀教师的水平，但它已经超过了普通教师的水平。AI可以作为普通教师的改进工具，并且应该让最优秀的教师参与开发AI，而不是依赖普通教师。此外，作者提到教育本身涉及社会控制的问题，特别是在讨论敏感历史和科学争议时，AI可能更客观。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是AI是否能被称为“导师”。[jjani]认为文章内容与标题不符，AI目前只是帮助完成作业，而非真正起到导师的作用。
• [spwa4]进一步讨论了教育中的深层次问题，如教师的知识水平和教学能力，提出AI可以替代普通教师，但最优秀的教师仍然不可或缺。
• [spwa4]还提到教育中的敏感话题和历史争议，如优生学和种族灭绝理论，认为AI可能在处理这些争议时更为客观。

整体来看，讨论的核心在于AI在教育中的实际应用及其替代教师的潜力，以及AI在处理教育敏感话题时的角色。

Title:
Do AI tutors empower or enslave learners? Toward a critical use of AI in education
Authors:
Lucile Favero
,
Juan-Antonio Pérez-Ortiz
,
Tanja Käser
,
Nuria Oliver
View a PDF of the paper titled Do AI tutors empower or enslave learners? Toward a critical use of AI in education, by Lucile Favero and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The increasing integration of AI tools in education presents both opportunities and challenges, particularly regarding the development of the students' critical thinking skills. This position paper argues that while AI can support learning, its unchecked use may lead to cognitive atrophy, loss of agency, emotional risks, and ethical concerns, ultimately undermining the core goals of education. Drawing on cognitive science and pedagogy, the paper explores how over-reliance on AI can disrupt meaningful learning, foster dependency and conformity, undermine the students' self-efficacy, academic integrity, and well-being, and raise concerns about questionable privacy practices. It also highlights the importance of considering the students' perspectives and proposes actionable strategies to ensure that AI serves as a meaningful support rather than a cognitive shortcut. The paper advocates for an intentional, transparent, and critically informed use of AI that empowers rather than diminishes the learner.

• [spwa4] 指出文章对AI的批评并不针对AI独有的问题，而是与资金和努力相关的普遍教育问题。作者认为，尽管AI可能无法达到最优秀教师的水平，但它已经超过了普通教师的水平。AI可以作为普通教师的改进工具，并且应该让最优秀的教师参与开发AI，而不是依赖普通教师。此外，作者提到教育本身涉及社会控制的问题，特别是在讨论敏感历史和科学争议时，AI可能更客观。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是AI是否能被称为“导师”。[jjani]认为文章内容与标题不符，AI目前只是帮助完成作业，而非真正起到导师的作用。
• [spwa4]进一步讨论了教育中的深层次问题，如教师的知识水平和教学能力，提出AI可以替代普通教师，但最优秀的教师仍然不可或缺。
• [spwa4]还提到教育中的敏感话题和历史争议，如优生学和种族灭绝理论，认为AI可能在处理这些争议时更为客观。

整体来看，讨论的核心在于AI在教育中的实际应用及其替代教师的潜力，以及AI在处理教育敏感话题时的角色。

data.author: -yukari
data.article_summary: Ceramic利用Haxe编程语言的特性，实现了一次编写代码，即可将其转译为C++、JavaScript或C#。这使得应用能够原生导出到多个平台，包括Windows、Mac、Linux、iOS、Android、HTML5/WebGL，甚至Unity项目。这种跨平台能力大大提升了开发效率和应用兼容性。了解更多关于Ceramic的信息可以通过相关链接。

data.title: Magic .env files built for sharing: Human-first, AI-friendly
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: Varlock 是一种用于管理环境变量和配置文件的工具，支持声明式 schema、秘密值保护和配置验证。它通过装饰器注释增强了 `.env` 文件的功能，提供强大的验证能力，并在开发周期早期捕获错误。Varlock 支持从外部来源安全地读取秘密值，自动生成类型，并允许组合默认配置和环境特定配置。此外，它可以作为 dotenv 的直接替代品，无需更改代码即可获得验证、安全性和其他增强功能。Varlock 还提供了便捷的安装方式和详细的入门文档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于管理环境变量和处理敏感信息的工具和方法的比较

不同观点：
• jelder的观点：
  - 认为`.env`文件不直观，管理环境变量的工作不应该由使用这些变量的进程来负责。
  - 推荐使用direnv工具（https://direnv.net），认为它更优，因为可以自动加载当前目录下的`.envrc`文件中的环境变量。
  - direnv具有丰富的标准库，可以方便地操作PATH等环境变量。
  - 对于敏感信息，通过在`.envrc`中添加`source_env_if_exists .envrc.private`行，并把`.envrc.private`加入`.gitignore`，来实现安全管理。

• Nullabillity的观点：
  - 对某些工具（如Varlock）声称“AI-friendly”表示质疑，认为这种说法模糊且无实际意义。
  - 对工具依赖1Password来管理敏感信息的做法表示担忧，认为这不一定合适或负责任。
  - 质疑工具声称能“始终在CLI输出中隐藏敏感值”的能力，指出工具可能无法控制外部应用的配置输出。

补充讨论：
- jelder强调了direnv的自动化和灵活性，特别是其对环境变量管理的便利性和安全性（通过分离公共和私有配置文件）。
- Nullabillity则关注工具对敏感信息管理的可靠性和安全性，对工具依赖第三方应用和宣传口号持怀疑态度。
- 争议的焦点在于如何安全且有效地管理环境变量和敏感信息，特别是在多工具和多环境协作的情况下。

data.title: Optimizing a Math Expression Parser in Rust
data.author: serial_dev
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在Rust中优化数学表达式解析器，逐步提升其速度和内存效率。初始版本耗时43.1秒，通过一系列优化最终减少到0.98秒。

### 优化步骤：
1. **避免向量分配**：将tokenize过程中的向量分配去除，耗时从43.1秒降至6.45秒。
2. **零分配**：直接从输入字节解析，耗时降至3.68秒。
3. **去除Peekable**：耗时降至3.21秒。
4. **多线程和SIMD**：耗时降至2.21秒。
5. **内存映射I/O**：最终耗时降至0.98秒。

每步优化都详细解释了具体做法和性能提升的原因，最终实现了一个高效的数学表达式解析器。完整代码可在GitHub上找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的split_whitespace性能、匹配优化、文件读取处理、流解析器、自然表达式解析器以及代码优化和基准测试的复杂性。

不同观点：
• **zokier** 认为 `split_whitespace` 每次调用都会分配中间切片，这可能会导致性能开销。他建议使用更直接的步骤，比如从 `&str` 转换到 `&[u8]`，并指出新的tokenizer没有处理空白字符，只是假设每个token后都有一个空白，这可能解释了速度提升的原因。

• **catfacts** 提到 `match` 比较的是字符串而不是字符，并推测Common Lisp在字符比较上可能更优化。他还对Rust的错误处理提出质疑，特别是文件读取错误时Rust的安全性，并建议学习Rust的适当处理方式，尽管他认为这类文章对学习Rust和优化非常有帮助。

• **conaclos** 对作者没有尝试实现流解析器表示惊讶，认为这样可以避免将整个文件加载到内存中，或者依赖内存映射文件等操作系统特性。

• **tialaramex** 提到自己正在写一个“自然”的算术表达式解析器，并分享了自己Rust项目中现有的解析功能和未来计划，认为这种练习对习惯不同解析方式很有帮助。

• **makapuf** 表示对这些优化文章的兴趣，并建议不仅要关注运行时间基准测试，还要考虑CPU时间、内存使用情况，以及代码复杂性（特别是为了少量速度提升而增加复杂性的取舍）。

• **ramon156** 认为这种优化主题非常适合作为课堂项目，让学生自由探索并学习不同的优化方法。

补充讨论：
• **amelius** 请求解释代码行 `n => Token::Operand(n.parse().unwrap())` 中编译器如何推导 `n` 的类型，这涉及到Rust的类型推导机制。

争议焦点：
• 对于 `split_whitespace` 是否会产生不必要的分配存在不同看法。
• Rust在文件读取和错误处理方面的安全性和处理方式引发讨论。
• 不同语言（如Rust和Common Lisp）在性能优化上的比较也是一个讨论焦点。

本文介绍了如何在Rust中优化数学表达式解析器，逐步提升其速度和内存效率。初始版本耗时43.1秒，通过一系列优化最终减少到0.98秒。

### 优化步骤：
1. **避免向量分配**：将tokenize过程中的向量分配去除，耗时从43.1秒降至6.45秒。
2. **零分配**：直接从输入字节解析，耗时降至3.68秒。
3. **去除Peekable**：耗时降至3.21秒。
4. **多线程和SIMD**：耗时降至2.21秒。
5. **内存映射I/O**：最终耗时降至0.98秒。

每步优化都详细解释了具体做法和性能提升的原因，最终实现了一个高效的数学表达式解析器。完整代码可在GitHub上找到。

data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 计算机科学家发现了一种方法可以证明谎言，揭示了区块链和其他数字加密方案中的一个显著安全问题。传统上，计算机程序依赖哈希函数来生成看似随机的数据，并假设这些输出与真正的随机性无异，这一假设被称为随机预言模型。然而，一篇新论文颠覆了这一基础假设，展示了一种欺骗商用证明系统来验证虚假陈述的方法。该系统在随机预言模型下是安全的，但研究人员发现，无论使用何种哈希函数生成“随机性”，他们都能够证明谎言。这一发现对区块链和加密货币交易等依赖此类证明协议的系统构成了威胁，因为这些系统需要通过外部服务器验证计算。该研究引发了对随机预言模型的重新思考，并凸显了修复这些漏洞的紧迫性。

By

An attack on a fundamental proof technique reveals a glaring security issue for blockchains and other digital encryption schemes.

All topics
Randomness is a source of power. From the coin toss that decides which team gets the ball to the random keys that secure online interactions, randomness lets us make choices that are fair and impossible to predict.
But in many computing applications, suitable randomness can be hard to generate. So instead, programmers often rely on things called hash functions, which swirl data around and extract some small portion in a way that looks random. For decades, many computer scientists have presumed that for practical purposes, the outputs of good hash functions are generally indistinguishable from genuine randomness — an assumption they call the random oracle model.
“It’s hard to find today a cryptographic application… whose security analysis does not use this methodology,” said
Ran Canetti
of Boston University.
Now, a
new paper
has shaken that bedrock assumption. It demonstrates a method for tricking a commercially available proof system into certifying false statements, even though the system is demonstrably secure if you accept the random oracle model. Proof systems related to this one are essential for the blockchains that record cryptocurrency transactions, where they are used to certify computations performed by outside servers.
There’s “a lot of money relying on this stuff,” said
Eylon Yogev
of Bar-Ilan University in Israel. For blockchain proof protocols, “there’s a huge motivation for attackers to break the security of the system.”
In the new paper — by
Dmitry Khovratovich
of the Ethereum Foundation,
Ron Rothblum
of the zero-knowledge proof technology company Succinct and the Technion in Haifa, Israel, and Lev Soukhanov of the blockchain-focused start-up [[alloc] init] — the researchers are able to prove lies no matter which hash function is used to generate the “randomness” the proof system relies upon.
When Yogev heard about the team’s result, he said, “I had the feeling that someone is pulling the carpet from under my feet.” He and others have been working to patch up these vulnerabilities. But “it’s far from being a solved issue,” he said.
More broadly, the new result is forcing a reckoning about the random oracle model. “This is a time to rethink,” Canetti said.
A Mathematical Blender
A host of different computing applications — from cryptocurrencies to cloud computing — involve convincing a bunch of strangers on the internet that you’ve performed a computation correctly. The new paper shows how to hijack a fundamental technique that enables people to certify such computations. The technique, called the Fiat-Shamir transformation, is useful not just in blockchains and cloud computing but also in many other cryptographic applications, such as the key exchanges that safeguard web transactions and encrypt text messages. It’s so ubiquitous that it has become a verb, as in “Let’s Fiat-Shamir this.”
Ron Rothblum, together with Dmitry Khovratovich and Lev Soukhanov, have upended the prevailing thinking on a fundamental proof technique.
Courtesy of Ron Rothblum
The Fiat-Shamir transformation is used in settings where you can verify a computation by inspecting it in random spots. For instance, if a professor has assigned 100 problems for homework but doesn’t want to grade a student’s entire assignment, she can randomly choose 10 problems to grade. In the language of computer scientists, she is making 10 “random challenges” to the student’s homework. If the answers to those 10 problems are correct, the professor can feel confident that most of the other answers are correct too. (There are ways to modify this setup if she wants to be convinced that the student got every single problem right, not just most of them.)
This particular scenario would probably play out on the professor’s desk. But since the Fiat-Shamir transformation is about convincing a bunch of distant strangers, let’s instead imagine that the student wants to prove the correctness of his homework not just to the professor, but to an entire auditorium full of people.
Imagine that the student starts by “turning in” his assignment by locking each of his answers in a separate box. Next, the professor picks 10 numbers out of a hat to determine her 10 random challenges. The student unlocks those 10 boxes, and the professor grades the contents. Since the student locked up his answers before knowing what

data.title: Radiocarbon dating reveals Rapa Nui not as isolated as previously thought
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 考古学研究通过放射性碳定年法揭示，复活节岛（Rapa Nui）并非之前认为的那样孤立。研究表明，波利尼西亚的仪式活动和纪念性建筑存在东西方双向传播。最初，人类从西波利尼西亚（如汤加和萨摩亚）向东迁徙，建立了包括复活节岛在内的定居点。然而，研究发现，东波利尼西亚的仪式场所（如马拉埃石台）在时间上早于西方，表明东方的仪式理念后来反馈影响了西方。这挑战了复活节岛孤立发展的传统观点，显示岛屿间存在复杂的互动网络。研究强调，尽管最初的迁徙是从西到东，但随后的文化发展更为复杂，存在东向西的影响。
